item.title: OpenAI Fixes ChatGPT Billing Error, Promises to Make it 40% Worse
item.description: OpenAI says a billing mistake made its new AI models cheaper to use than intended. Subscribers will now burn through their allowances faster, but get a free one-time usage reset.

item.title: Ary Borges on Arthur Elias: “He works with us and understands players”
item.description: Ary Borges on Arthur Elias: “He works with us and understands players” Alongside her strong form at Angel City and her string of call-ups to the Brazilian national team, motherhood has brought a new chapter to Ary Borges’ journey. At a press conference on Thursday (26), the midfielder highlighted the support she received from head coach Arthur Elias and spoke about the importance of his understanding when he left her out of October’s international window so she could spend the first days of her newborn daughter Melanie’s life alongside her wife, Gabriela. “This is a very special time for me. Arthur is a very caring person who really values relationships, both individually and as a group. In this situation, he showed once again how much he stands by us and understands the players. Arthur watched me grow at Centro Olímpico, and now he has watched me become a mother,” she said. “Before the last squad announcement, he called me, asked about my family and was very honest with me. He said that my saying no at that moment (to joining the squad) was actually saying yes. As athletes, we give up so much, and he gave me peace of mind to enjoy a special moment with my family. He also reassured other players who want to become mothers but worry it could affect their careers,” she added. Ary Borges during a Brazilian women’s national team training session in Hiroshima, Japan Credit: Luciana Vermell/CBF Ary has known Arthur Elias since her days at Centro Olímpico, where she played between 2015 and 2016. As a youngster, she would talk with her teammates about the possibility of being a ball girl at matches involving the team he coached. Years later, he would become her coach with the Brazilian national team and her nemesis in matches between Corinthians and Palmeiras, as she played for Palmeiras from 2020 to 2022, during a period of Corinthians dominance. Among the players called up for this international window, Ary logged the most playing time for her club, Angel City in the United States. She made 28 appearances and played 2,688 minutes, figures that underline her consistent involvement throughout the season. Speaking about the challenges facing Brazil in Japan, the midfielder highlighted the importance of the friendlies against the hosts as part of their World Cup preparations. “We’re very happy to be here in Japan and experience a different culture. Our profession gives us that privilege. In football terms, Japan are opponents who present us with plenty of challenges. This is another opportunity for us to study, improve and work toward our main goal, which is getting closer and closer (the World Cup). These have all the makings of two very interesting games, and I hope that, just like last time, we come away with two wins,” she said. item.title: ‘I bought a book on how to have a boy-child’ – Makinde
item.description: By Angel Aniobi Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde has revealed that he bought a book and ovulation kits with his wife in their attempt to have a male child after welcoming two daughters. Makinde made this disclosure during an interview with media personality Chude Jideonwo, where he spoke about his family, fatherhood and the decision to have a third child. Recounting how they planned their family, the governor said he initially wanted just one child but reluctantly agreed to have two after his wife questioned why they should have only one. According to him, he was comfortable with having two daughters and did not consider the gender of his children important. “Gender doesn’t mean anything to me because I felt whether a girl or a boy, it’s all linked up to how you’re going to bring them up and how you set them up to impact their environment, and you can do it with any kid,” he said. Makinde, however, explained that cultural expectations and comments from his mother-in-law amplified his wife’s desire to have a male child. He said his mother-in-law told his wife that Yoruba men whose wives did not give birth to boys could seek to have a male child outside their marriages. “I’m a Yoruba man, but I think I am okay with the girls that God has blessed us with,” he recalled saying. The governor disclosed that it took more than five years for him to understand his wife’s desire to have a son, after which they agreed to explore ways of having a male child. He said he subsequently purchased a book on how to conceive a boy, which they both read and followed, alongside purchasing ovulation kits. “So, I said, okay, well, that’s fine. We have to go and buy a book on how to have a boy, and then we’ll read it and apply strictly,” he said. Makinde added that their efforts eventually resulted in the birth of their son, who became their third child. “That was it. That was what produced the boy, and I was finally left off the hook,” he said. Vanguard News The post ‘I bought a book on how to have a boy-child’ – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Rams grind out 26-13 win over Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
item.description: Nov 25, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images INGLEWOOD, Calif. — Blake Corum turned 26 on Wednesday and celebrated with a career-best performance, carrying the ball 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams controlled the clock and the trenches in a 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers . It was the NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, and the Rams used it to extend their winning streak to five and improve to 7-4. Corum’s 32 carries were the most by a Rams running back in Sean McVay’s decade in charge. He scored for the seventh straight game, and Kyren Williams added a touchdown and 46 yards on 12 carries as Los Angeles finished with 241 rushing yards. Brandon McManus contributed four field goals. Matthew Stafford needed only 16 completions on 23 attempts for 140 yards (and one interception) as the Rams leaned on the ground game against an injury-thinned receiving corps. The teams were tied 13-13 at halftime. Green Bay had clawed back from an early deficit behind a Christian Watson touchdown catch, but the second half belonged entirely to the Rams. Los Angeles outscored the Packers 13-0 after the break, held Green Bay to just 55 rushing yards, and dominated time of possession (40:40 to 19:20). Jordan Love finished 17-of-29 for 198 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. The Packers fell to 6-5 after their second straight loss. The night was not without controversy. Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson late in the second quarter; Watson was ruled out with a concussion after catching four passes for 65 yards and the score. Micah Parsons, returning from a torn ACL, recorded a sack for Green Bay, but the Packers could not generate consistent offense once the Rams established their rushing rhythm. The result carries clear playoff weight. Both teams entered at 6-4 in a crowded NFC wild-card race; the head-to-head win and the possession edge now give the Rams a clearer path. Los Angeles hosts the Kansas City Chiefs next, while Green Bay travels to face the New Orleans Saints.

item.title: Jackson’s Future In Miami Looks Grim Despite Sunday’s Start
item.description: Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins are staring down a massive decision at right tackle, and the writing is on the wall for Austin Jackson. Yahoo Sports NFL reports that Jackson is in the last year of his contract while the coaching staff actively weighs a change at the position. This is a bad week and likely the end of his time in South Florida. Proctor Stays Put for Now While some reports suggest Proctor is the heir apparent to the right tackle spot, Head Coach Jeff Hafley shut down that talk before practice on Wednesday. Per Sports Illustrated , Proctor will not be moving to right tackle this week and might not make the switch at all this season. The team is sticking with Jackson for now, barring an injury that forces him out of the upcoming game against the New York Jets. Hafley did not say exactly what is wrong with Jackson, only that the player would be limited in practice on Wednesday. The coach added that Jackson is expected to line up at his spot at right tackle when the Jets visit Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday. This leaves the Dolphins in a weird spot, relying on a player who has struggled all season while holding a rookie guard back from his natural progression. Looking Beyond the Current Roster The front office is clearly weighing long-term options while trying to win the next game. If the team moves on from Jackson, they have seen other players step up elsewhere in the league. Chukwuebuka Godrick started three games for the Kansas City Chiefs last season, and Caedan Wallace has two career starts on his resume with the New England Patriots. Wallace started one game at left tackle and the other as a sixth offensive lineman, showing he can handle different roles. The Dolphins also have a pass rush to worry about on the other side of the ball. Rookie pass rusher David Bailey is the second overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft and is tied for third in the NFL with 9.5 sacks. During their first meeting in Week 7, the Dolphins limited him to four tackles and half a sack over 61 snaps, with Bailey recording those statistics. The team faces the Jets this Sunday at 1 p.m.

item.title: Detroit Tigers Sign Two Familiar Faces
item.description: The Detroit Tigers are bringing back a pair of familiar faces just one week after parting ways with them. According to Tigers beat writer Evan Woodbery of MLive, the organization has signed infielder Trey Sweeney and left-handed pitcher Jake Miller to minor-league contracts after non-tendering both players last week. The moves allow Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris to retain both players without committing spots on the 40-man roster. It is a strategy that has become somewhat familiar during Harris’ tenure in Detroit. Sep 23, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Detroit Tigers shortstop Trey Sweeney (27) throws to first in the third inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Tigers Re-Sign Trey Sweeney and Jake Miller Both signings are confirmed on the Tigers’ official transaction page , which lists the moves as taking place on November 25. Sweeney and Miller had been among the four players Detroit designated for assignment on November 17 before officially becoming free agents. Sweeney, 26, provides the Tigers with additional infield depth as he works to reestablish himself following an injury-plagued 2026 campaign. Although there is no guarantee he will return to the major league roster, keeping him in the organization makes sense for Detroit. Meanwhile, Miller, 25, is an intriguing left-handed pitching prospect who missed a significant portion of last season with a hip injury. According to NBC Sports , Miller posted a 0.77 ERA and struck out 24 batters across 23 1/3 minor-league innings in 2026. Scott Harris Continues Familiar Roster-Building Strategy As Woodbery pointed out Thursday morning, Harris has had considerable success convincing players who have been non-tendered to return to the Tigers on minor-league contracts. The strategy allows Detroit to retain organizational depth while maintaining flexibility on its 40-man roster. Sweeney and Miller were two of the three players the Tigers non-tendered ahead of last week’s deadline , with outfielder Matt Vierling being the other. Whether Vierling could eventually return to the organization remains to be seen. Neither signing is going to generate the excitement of a major free-agent acquisition, but these are the types of low-risk moves that can pay dividends over the course of a 162-game season. In Miller’s case, particularly, there is enough upside to make bringing him back a worthwhile investment.

item.title: WNBA’s 2027 Cap Math Leaves Little Room For Error For Dream
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The WNBA salary cap rules for 2027 create a harsh reality for teams trying to build a winner. The Atlanta Dream faces a math problem that leaves almost no room for maneuvering. According to Sports Illustrated , the league cap can rise by no more than 13% to $7.91 million. This small jump does not help teams that already have limited space. The Dream must sign three new players just to fill their roster. Each of these new signings costs at least $280,800. That adds up fast and eats into the money available for star talent. The Minimum Salary Trap Every team must keep 12 players on the roster during the season. This rule forces franchises to spend money they might prefer to save. Per Sports Illustrated, the lowest full-season minimum salary for a player with no experience is $280,800 in 2027. The Dream already has nine players under contract totaling about $6.18 million. To reach the required 12 players, the team needs to spend an extra $842,400 on new signings. This mandatory spending pushes their total obligations to $7.02 million. The math leaves the team with very little flexibility to sign big free agents. Where the Money Goes The gap between the total cap and what a team can actually spend is now wider than ever. The Atlanta Dream will have to spend $7.02 million just to meet basic roster requirements. This leaves them with about $886,000 to spend freely on top-tier talent. That amount is tiny compared to the cost of a supermax deal. A supermax salary is 20% of the cap for a given year, which would be roughly $1.58 million. Only the current club or, in the event of free agency, the former club can sign an eligible player to a supermax. This restriction makes it hard for other teams to poach stars from the Dream without paying a premium. Spending Limits and Roster Rules A team’s payroll cannot surpass the salary cap at any moment unless it applies a hardship, emergency hardship, pregnancy/childbirth, or season-ending injury exception. For any specific year, the standard maximum salary equals 17% of the salary cap. These tight limits mean teams cannot simply throw money at every problem. They must plan carefully or risk breaking the rules. The Dream’s situation shows how the new rules squeeze out spending power. With only $886,000 left for free spending, the team has very few options to improve the roster beyond the minimums. The Dream, in its present form, must spend $7.02 million, which leaves approximately $886,000 available for unrestricted spending above minimum salaries.

item.title: Why do the Lions and Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving?
item.description: Detroit Lions fans dress for Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears, Thursday, Nov. 28, 2019 at Ford Field. Detroit Lions fans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did that come to be? The Lions played their first Thanksgiving game in 1934. It was their first season in Detroit. They had previously been located in Portsmouth, Ohio, where they were known as the Portsmouth Spartans. A radio executive named George Richards bought the franchise and moved it to Detroit. The Lions were having difficulty gaining any sort of popularity in their new home city. Richards came up with the idea of scheduling their team’s big game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. The Lions were 10-1 at the time, and the Bears were 11-0. This was before the days when the league dictated the schedule to its teams. The teams themselves could schedule the times of their games. Richards used his connections in the radio business to get the game broadcast nationally. Even thought Detroit lost, it was a huge success. The Lions sold the game out, and they have played on Thanksgiving ever since with the exception of World War II years despite some calls for them to lose the game during the dismal Matt Millen Era. Thanksgiving gained a second traditional team in 1951. For the next thirteen years, the Green Bay Packers traveled to Detroit to play the Lions on Thanksgiving. Vince Lombardi ended the arrangement. Lombardi cited the end of an agreement that paid the Packers $10,000 extra for playing the game, the difficulties of playing games on a short week every year, and having to face a rival in front of an electric crowd on the road every season. Of course since the teams are in the same division, the Packers remain a frequent Thanksgiving opponent for Detroit. So how about the Cowboys? In the mid-1960’s the NFL was looking to add a second Thanksgiving game. It was not entirely clear it would work outside Detroit, where Thanksgiving NFL was already a tradition. The Dallas Cowboys were a six year old team with no history of winning. General manager Tex Schramm was a visionary. (He was a driving force behind other innovations like instant replay, the flags on goal posts, the NFL-AFL merger, and too many others to name). He jumped at the opportunity. The Cowboys hosted their first Thanksgiving game in 1966. They kept the game annually until the 1970’s when the league hatched a plan to alternate between the Cowboys and the then St. Louis Cardinals . The Cowboys were to host the second game in even years and the Cardinals in odd years. The Cardinals only hosted two home Thanksgiving games, however, which took place in 1975 and in 1977. item.title: How to watch: Tennessee vs. Iowa State in the Players Era 16
item.description: Nov 24, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Tennessee guard Terrence Hill Jr. (3) runs the offense as Maryland guard D.J. Wagner (2) defends during the second half of an opening round game of the Players Era Sixteen tournament at Michelob Ultra Arena. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tennessee has advanced to the Players Era 16 Tournament Michelob Ultra Arena semifinals following an opening round win over Maryland. The Volunteers were powered by Dai Dai Ames against the Terps, who poured in 24 points off the bench to spark Tennessee to a 72-64 win. Now with the MUA bracket down to four, Tennessee will face Iowa State for the right to play for the bracket title on Friday. The T-Mobile Arena bracket is down to TCU, Creighton, Baylor and Gonzaga. The winners of each bracket will square off on Saturday for the Players Era 16 title. Thursday serves as a Sweet 16 rematch from March, where Tennessee got the better of the Cyclones. Of course, the rosters have completely changed since then, although Iowa State is still led by senior point guard Tamin Lipsey. One thing has remained the same for TJ Otzelberger — they’ll turn you over. Iowa State is tenth in the nation in turnovers forced with 19 per game. The winner here advances to face the winner of St. Johns-Louisville. The losers will play in the third place game on Friday. item.title: Christian Pulisic, Antoine Griezmann and Emma Hayes’ USWNT: Why American soccer fans have plenty to celebrate this Thanksgiving
item.description: Thanksgiving 2026 GFX - GOAL GOAL breaks down what you should be thankful for during this holiday season. It's Thanksgiving, and we all know what that means. Turkey, gravy, mashed potatoes, stuffing - all on the menu. There's plenty to be thankful for, but that doesn't just extend to food; it extends to soccer, too. Obviously, there are more important things in life to give thanks for at this time of year, but it is also worth acknowledging the sport's role in everyday life. For some, it's an obsession. For others, it's a distraction. But, if you're reading this story, it's safe to assume that you're glad that soccer is a part of your life in some way. So, with that in mind, let's sit down, put down the fork for a moment and give thanks for all of the good things about American soccer and, just as crucially, all of the things worth being excited for on the horizon, too. The 2026 World Cup Spain helped make the 2026 World Cup a summer to remember as fans from across the globe came together in America. Yeah, it's over now, but what a ride it was! For one summer, soccer came stateside and, for one summer, America was at the forefront of the beautiful game. The scenes were unforgettable: the games, the pageantry, the fans sweeping through cities. Scotland in Boston, Algeria in Kansas, Norway's Viking Row taking over Times Square - it was a wonderfully unifying experience, one that saw fans from all over the world experience American hospitality. It also saw Americans experience a taste of the unknown as they learned about those who had arrived for a summer of fun. From a USMNT perspective, yes, the ending was rough, but the road there was full of highs. The wins over Paraguay and Australia were unlike anything the world had seen from an American team. The Turkey game, despite the defeat, had several feel-good moments. Even the Bosnia and Herzegovina game that began the downturn was full of both grit and talent that inspired onlookers all over the world. So, before we turn the page, a toast to the 2026 World Cup and a thank you to all who made it special. Copa America, Olympics and Women's World Cup on the way More tournaments will soon be arriving on American shores. And, if you liked the World Cup experience, get ready for more, because there's more coming. Just this week, it was confirmed that both the 2031 Women's World Cup and 2028 Copa America will be coming to the U.S., bringing two more major tournaments stateside. You can also tack on the 2028 Olympics, too, giving fans another huge competition worth being excited to watch for both the men's and women's sides. For years, many looked at the 2026 World Cup as the pinnacle, the end of one era of American soccer. It turns out that wasn't the case; it was a huge, huge part, yes, but it was merely the latest step on a journey that, thankfully, includes plenty of big games stateside. American stars in big places For big names to keep that recognition, they need to put themselves on the biggest stage

item.title: Top 5 college football games to watch in Week 13
item.description: The final week of the 2026 college football regular season is here and "Rivalry Week", as it is lovingly known, is sure to deliver on Thanksgiving weekend. After Week 12 gave us some thrilling and unexpected results, a major shakeup to the month of November has left us with a delicious Week 13 slate. Though some of the more well-known rivalries aren't as interesting this year as they have been in years past, it just means that some more under-the-radar rivalry games will get their moment in the sun this week. It's also the last full weekend of the season with every team still playing. Everyone who gets to play after this week of games has earned it. Here at Sooners Wire, we'll be all over the big game on the docket for the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend , and it's just one of many exciting matchups in a very interesting group of regular-season finales. Here are the top five games to watch in Week 13. 1. USC at UCLA, Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT USC and UCLA haven't both been this good at the same time in a while, and they'll face off in Pasadena in a game that is extremely important to the Big Ten title game race. The Trojans are still technically alive in the standings to get to the conference championship game, but head coach Lincoln Riley's team would need a lot of help to get there. Instead, they're hoping for a convincing win and some chaos in front of them to allow them to sneak into the College Football Playoff as an at-large team. Quarterback Jayden Maiava and the offense will need to be on-point against a very strong defense. The Bruins saw their unbeaten season fall apart in last week's loss to Michigan, and new head coach Bob Chesney has had to navigate several quarterback injuries this season. Starter Nico Iamaleava went down weeks ago, with backup Ty Diffenbach filling in nicely in his stead. When Diffenbach was injured last week, Madden Iamaleava was forced into action, and the offense faltered. Diffenbach could potentially be in line to return this week, and this team can go to the Big Ten title game if they get a home win in the Rose Bowl on Saturday. 2. Oklahoma at Missouri, Saturday at 3:15 p.m. CT Oklahoma and Missouri play in the SEC's biggest game this week, as both programs have navigated treacherous schedules to land themselves in a good position heading into the final week of the regular season. The Sooners have won three straight games after a 4-4 start, and head coach Brent Venables has his team one win away from another undefeated November. Quarterback John Mateer has rebounded over the last three weeks, and he's playing confident football again. It's not in time to get OU to the CFP, but he's looking to finish strong on the road in Columbia. The Tigers are also out of the CFP race, but after beating Kentucky last week, they're also looking to finish the season on a high note. Head coach Eliah Drinkwitz can still put his team in a very good bowl game, and this squad can play like one of the SEC's best when they're on their g

item.title: Tiger Woods is making another comeback. Can his battered body hold up this time? | Opinion
item.description: How the other half lives, huh? I was reading one of those “day in the life” articles over the weekend, and it featured some guy called Scotch McClure, who is a big shot in the multibillion-dollar world of longevity tech, although his name does sound like something you’d find on the drink specials at my local bar. Anyway, ahead of another busy day at work, Scotch gets up at the crack of dawn every morning to meditate. “It’s how I align my chakras and bring my body and mind into coherence,” declared Scotch. I’m not sure what, or where, my own chakras are. My wife suggested they might be in that junk drawer with the Allen wrenches and obsolete phone chargers. But if I do stumble upon them, I can guarantee the damn things won’t be aligned. In fact, forget about aligning my chakras. I have enough trouble with the alignment in the setup of my golf swing, as the whole process, and inevitably disastrous results, drags my body and mind into complete incoherence. On the subject of the swing, I saw another article about research conducted by university psychologists that found golfers who think too much about technique can actually hurt their game. If it’s any help to the researchers, I’d like to add that the process of swinging a club at a ball is considerably easier when you don’t have any technique worth thinking about in the first place. I should be a psychologist, huh? More: What can we expect from Tiger Woods at the Hero? A review of his returns after long layoffs Next week, meanwhile, we’ll all get to see Tiger Woods swinging a club again for the first time in ages. You probably heard the news the other day that Tiger is set to make comeback No. 146, or something like that, in the 20-man, no-cut Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas. Now, I know Woods used to dabble in a bit of meditation, but since his last competitive appearance in the 2024 Open at Royal Troon, there have been a few hits to the coherence of both body and mind. Those chakras have been all over the place. Three more surgeries, two on his back and one on his Achilles, added to the wear and tear on a body that creaks like an abandoned ship, while yet another car accident, a subsequent DUI charge and a stint in an inpatient rehab facility in Switzerland provided more dispiriting twists to the turbulent Tiger tale. But after all the trials and tribulations, it looks like he’ll be back. Again. Will it be another short-lived exercise in futility? Who knows, but rightly or wrongly, a good chunk of the golf world will no doubt be captivated by this latest, tentative return to competition. Nobody cranks up the “will he, won’t he” drama quite like Tiger. I realize, of course, that many of you reading this probably couldn’t care less about another Woods comeback. In fact, you may have stopped reading this column already. Can you keep going, please? There are only 500 or so words left. item.title: 'Don't you change': Bill Cowher praises Dan Campbell
item.description: Credit: CBS Sports Dan Campbell has made Thanksgiving football much more enjoyable for millions of people across the country by making the Detroit Lions more competitive in recent years. The way he has led his team has won over even more fans along the way , including former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and NFL Today analyst Bill Cowher. When you think of Dan Campbell, you think of him as the ultimate football tough guy. But he hasn’t been afraid to wear his heart on his sleeve . And when Cowher gave him his flowers for an interview for The NFL Today on CBS ahead of the Lions hosting the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day, he couldn’t help but get emotional. This is awesome Dan Campbell got emotional when @CowherCBS gave him his flowers #nflt https://t.co/Zg2IFfrBwv — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) November 25, 2026 “I’d love to give thanks to you and what you represent, the journey that you’ve taken from a player to an assistant coach to climbing that ladder and landing here in Detroit; you embody what this place is all about. Yeah, you speak about resiliency, that’s Dan Campbell. You speak about grit, that’s Dan Campbell. You think about passion, that’s Dan Campbell,” Cowher said. “Thank you for being you. You’re authentic, man. And I don’t want you to ever change. Not only in the National Football League but this city, we need more people like Dan Campbell to continue to be a part of this society. As you keep your strive and pursuit for excellence is what’s made this country great, and you represent every element of that. Thank you for being you, and don’t you dare change. You bite the knees off on your way to getting that championship. Don’t you change, man.” After seeing Bill Cowher coach up Dan Campbell like that, with the emotion and intensity and pride on his own face, it’s almost a shame that the former Steelers coach never did return to the sidelines after his retirement after the 2006 season. That was an inspiring, powerful message. If you could ever get the two of them in the same locker room, players would run through any brick wall they could. The post Dan Campbell emotional over praise from Bill Cowher appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Driver Arrested Over Crash, Inferno That Killed 31 In Egypt
item.description: Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people . The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. This video grab taken from UGC images posted on social media on November 25, 2026, shows flames engulfing the area during a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Footage from the scene showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists on the ring road sounded their horns and struggled to get away. The prosecution said an investigation is underway to determine the driver’s criminal liability. The health ministry put the final toll at 31 dead and 21 wounded. More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. With its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Car crashes are common and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance, and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency. Flames And Smoke In 2018, the government issued a decision banning heavy transport vehicles from accessing the ring road around Greater Cairo from 6:00 am to midnight. Emergency services personnel and bystanders gather beside the wreckage of a tanker truck following a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate, on November 25, 2026. Photo by MAHMOUD EL-KHAWAS / AFP Wednesday’s disaster occurred at around 7:00 pm — at a time when the road was packed with pedestrians, buses and cars. Traffic had returned to normal in the early hours of Thursday after rescue operations ended and the wreckage of the truck and burned-out cars was cleared. “We were driving on the flyover above the ring road and saw flames rising to a height I can’t even describe,” said Wagih Ragheb, a witness to the disaster. “Then the explosions started… We got out of the car and went down to the ring road and found a catastrophic situation: buses and cars completely charred, and many dead.” Footage posted online by passersby showed people pulling others out of their cars in the inferno that erupted after the truck overturned. “We have a problem with our roads. These accidents happen very often, and no one knows how to solve this,” said Abdel Rahman Ahmed, who was at a Cairo hospital to donate blood for the wounded. item.title: The One Reason Nintendo and Rockstar Can Make Games Like Ocarina of Time and GTA 6
item.description: Though wildly different in tone and scope, both Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto 6 and Nintendo’s remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time exemplify the craft of making video games at its finest. Each one is redolent with attention to detail. Whether it’s the achingly nostalgic aesthetic of Ocarina or Rockstar’s Borg-like hive-mind of interconnected gameplay systems, there is a staggering amount of talent and dedication on display in these games. There are the kinds of endeavors that take years to pull off — and a company dedicated to helping its employees learn and grow over time. These are not the sort of games that can be produced by a company that lays people off every six months.

item.title: Packers most to blame for deflating Thanksgiving eve loss to Rams
item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Packers most to blame for deflating Thanksgiving eve loss to Rams appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers met their nightmare scenario in Week 12. Green Bay no-showed against Los Angeles in a 26-13 beatdown on Thanksgiving Eve. This tough loss will have a number of negative impacts on the Packers moving forward . Not only did Green Bay fall behind in the NFC North division standings, but they also lost to a team they’ll be competing with for a wild card spot in the NFC playoffs. The Rams now boast a head-to-head tiebreaker with the Packers. If both teams are fighting over one playoff spot at the end of the season, the Rams will win that tie. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur did not hold back his feelings when talking about what this loss means for this team after the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It’s extremely disappointing,” LaFleur admitted. “Like I told the team, it’s always 1-0, but we’re in a 1-game season from here on out. We dug ourselves a hole.” So what exactly went wrong on Wednesday night? And where does Green Bay go from here after falling to 6-5 on the season? Here are the Packers most to blame for their crushing Thanksgiving Eve loss to the Rams. Packers pass game couldn’t create chunk plays, made too many mistakes Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images The X-factor that has kept Green Bay competitive this season was their explosive passing attack. Unfortunately, it completely vanished on Thanksgiving Eve. The Packers only managed 189 passing yards against the Rams. Green Bay’s inability to create huge chunk plays through the air completely neutralized their attack, turning the game into a low-scoring slugfest. Love’s pair of interceptions in the second half did not help matters at all. His first interception was arguably the more devastating turnover. Green Bay was driving inside LA territory down by just one score at 20-13. Sadly, that interception caused a huge momentum swing and took away Green Bay’s best chance at scoring points in the second half. The second interception was bad too, but the first one set the Rams on their path to victory. It is worth noting that Christian Watson left this game with a concussion . His absence made it easy for LA to lock down Matthew Golden on route deep down the field. At this point, it is unclear how long it will take for him to clear the NFL’s concussion protocol. But that’s a worry for another day. Green Bay made the smart decision to air the ball out against LA. Remember, the Rams are without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. So there was a path for the Packers to run away with this game if the passing game started cooking. Instead, it turned to disaster. If the Packers cannot bully a team like the Rams, how will they fare against an actually elite offense that can run up the points? item.title: How the Mets’ plans at first base look after signing Paul Goldschmidt
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 30: Jared Young #29 of the New York Mets gets set against the Houston Astros during the game at Citi Field on August 30, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caean Couto/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Mets coming to terms with Paul Goldschmidt on a one-year deal, the club has seemingly finished shopping for first baseman, their position of greatest need outside of pitching when the offseason began. The team looks poised to employ a platoon at first for the 2027 season. Before diving further into the position, let’s look at how we got here. The Mets entered the offseason looking to improve at first base, or at least fortify the position, while most of their remaining position player needs were mostly met. New York has been linked to a few players, most notably Ty France and Alec Bohm, but both players required multi-year commitments, and with France coming off a career year, he was very likely to cash in beyond what the Mets felt comfortable paying him. The Mets were previously interested in Teruaki Sato, who is not a first baseman by trade but would very likely have shifted across the infield had he signed here. With Sato signing a six-year deal with the Cubs, that option is now off the table. That brings us to where we are now. After letting Pete Alonso leave for Baltimore last offseason, the Mets decided to replace him with Jorge Polanco, who had never previously played first but profiled as someone who could manage the position and who was coming off his best season by wRC+ (132) and his third-best by fWAR (2.6). I don’t really need to recount how poorly his first season in Queens went, but let’s just say it was an unmitigated disaster and leave it at that. On the positive side, Jared Young really blossomed in his age-30 season and proved to be a great stop-gap at the position, so much so that he worked his way into the team’s plans for 2027. Entering the offseason, the team had, theoretically, three first basemen on the roster—Young, Polanco, and Mark Vientos, who was tendered a contract prior to the deadline. The rest of their infield appears locked in, with Bo Bichette manning third after exercising his player option, Marcus Semien under contract for two more years, and Francisco Lindor still holding down the short stop position for New York after an injury-plagued and down year. So how do the Mets handle first base in 2027? Well, as mentioned, the Goldschmidt signing all but confirms that the team will employ a lefty-righty platoon, and they seem to have the right guys to do it. Goldschmidt mashed against left-handed pitchers last year, hitting .299/.393/.573 with a 168 wRC+ in 157 at-bats (for comparison, he hit .213/.239/.351 with a 60 wRC+ in 188 at-bats against righties). Young, meanwhile, excelled against righties, slashing .275/.339/.454 with a 120 wRC+ in 251 at-bats (when facing righties, he hit .228/.290/.316 with a 72 wRC+. They were also both solid defensively, with both Young and Goldschmidt finis

item.title: Thursday Rockpile: The worst case scenario in the Rockies latest trade is… not that bad
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - MAY 28: Davis Martin #65 of the Chicago White Sox celebrates against the Minnesota Twins at Rate Field on May 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming into the offseason, two things were clear about the Rockies: They had a desperate organization wide need for pitching . They had 2027 payroll space available . Over the past week the Rockies have been very busy leveraging that payroll space in order to address their pitching needs. Yesterday, Thomas Harding reported that the Rockies have signed LHP David Peterson to a two-year, $32 million dollar deal. Not long after, Jeff Passan reported that they had also signed LHP Patrick Sandoval to a three-year $42 million dollar deal. Look for more on those signings in the coming days. But for now, take a moment to consider the move the Rockies made last week when they began addressing that need for pitching by spending some of their 2027 money in an unusual way: making a trade with the Chicago White Sox for Davis Martin and Luis Castillo . It’s a fascinating trade that saw the Rockies take on the entirety of the $22.75 million owed to Castillo in 2027 in order to get four years of Martin. For the White Sox, this deal made sense because they needed to maximize every dollar spent this year with their limited budget and playoff aspirations. The Rockies, however, do not have that financial pressure in 2027 and used that difference as leverage to gain talent for, essentially, just money. Having had some time to reflect on the deal, however, I think the most interesting aspect is how the worst-case scenario for this trade just isn’t meaningfully bad for the Rockies. By far the largest cost the Rockies paid in this trade is taking on Castillo’s contract. The majority of the baseball world has written off Castillo after his abysmal 2026 performance. That’s understandable given how his underlying data had been trending slowly downward for the past few seasons before falling off a cliff last year. The narrative is obvious: Castillo has simultaneously seen his fastballs lose velocity and his breaking balls lose spin, but some of the effect of this decline was masked by his transition from a very hitter-friendly home venue (Great American Ballpark in Cincinnati) to the most pitcher-friendly home venue in MLB (T-Mobile Park in Seattle) in 2022. This past season, the slow decline reached a breaking point when mixed with ongoing shoulder issues and a move to a less pitcher-friendly home ballpark in Chicago. That multi-year trend in the wrong direction made the bottom falling out in terms of Castillo’s topline results last season seem less like an outlier season in an otherwise stellar career and more like the end of one. Given all of that, it is understandable why both the Mariners and the White Sox were so desperate to stop paying Castillo the money he is owed (and earned with his early career performance). item.title: NFLSU rookie check-in: Week 12
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: AJ Haulcy #25 of the Indianapolis Colts runs against the Indianapolis Colts prior to an NFL football game at NRG Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images CB Mansoor Delane Delane was able to bounce back from his injury woes and was dominant against the Cardinals. He didn’t make any crazy plays, but he also didn’t make mistakes, which is exactly what you want from a CB1. The Chiefs will be playing on Thanksgiving against the Buffalo Bills, which will be the biggest game of Delane’s early career. Safety A.J. Haulcy We finally got the A.J. Haulcy game. The rookie showed out against the Houston Texans, ending the game with an impressive interception and led the team in run stops. Indianapolis still got destroyed in this game, like usual, but Haulcy truly stood out. Next game will be against the New York Giants, another game where Haulcy can get a turnover. WR Zavion Thomas Next up is Zavion Thomas, and he had a really good game last week. He had two receptions for 56 yards, with one being a huge completion for the Bears, and he also got a 30-yard run. In the battle with Barion Brown, who we will get to, Thomas was utilized much better and did really well when called upon. Another one of our Thanksgiving games, Thomas and the Bears will be playing against the Detroit Lions, and maybe Thomas can have yet another big play. TE Bauer Sharp It was nice to see Sharp get a target this week, but once again, we are not seeing enough usage. WR Barion Brown As I mentioned earlier, Thomas and Brown faced off last week, and Thomas clearly won. Brown had some moments on special teams, but his usage on offense wasn’t great, and he did much worse on an identical run that Thomas took for 30 yards. The Saints offense is all over the place, so Brown will need to rely on special teams to make a difference. LB Harold Perkins The Falcons were on their bye week, and their first game back will be against the Minnesota Vikings. It will be the Kirk Cousins revenge game, so now it’s Perkins’ job to stop that from happening. QB Garrett Nussmeier Did not play because Patrick Mahomes is healthy. EDGE Jack Pyburn Did not play.

item.title: Recruiting Roundup: 2 newest commits explains why they chose Michigan Football
item.description: Welcome to the Recruiting Roundup, our twice-per-week series breaking down the latest developments on the recruiting trail for the Michigan Wolverines. We’ll keep you up to date on the top targets, the visits they take, the predictions that analysts make, and everything in between. Here’s what you need to know today… Michigan’s two-way plans sold Jerrimiah Cross 2028 three-star athlete Jerrimiah Cross grew up rooting for Michigan. When it came time to pick a school, the Wolverines gave the River Rouge junior another reason to stay home. They were one of the few programs willing to give him a shot at both wide receiver and cornerback. Cross chose Michigan over Michigan State, Arizona State and Virginia Tech on Tuesday, becoming the Wolverines’ first commitment in the 2028 class. The Rivals Industry Rankings list him as the No. 119 receiver nationally and the No. 23 prospect in Michigan. “I’m comfortable playing wherever the team needs me, but I know they like me at both receiver and corner,” Cross told The Michigan Insider’s Brice Marich . Cross gave Michigan plenty of film to work with at both spots this fall. He caught 51 passes for 910 yards and 12 touchdowns. At corner, he made 32 tackles, broke up seven passes, forced two fumbles and picked off two passes. Landon Hall goes from a playoff comeback to a Michigan commitment Last Friday, Landon Hall had two minutes to erase an 11-point deficit and keep Mishawaka (Ind.) Penn’s undefeated season alive. He pulled it off, leading Penn to a 49-45 win and a spot in the state title game. The next day, his brothers watched as Kyle Whittingham offered him a scholarship on his first visit to Michigan. “Their main reason was that I was a winner,” Hall told The Wolverine’s Ethan McDowell . Hall initially planned to get through Friday’s state championship game before turning his attention back to recruiting. By Wednesday, he’d made up his mind. The three-star quarterback committed to Michigan, joining Kamden Lopati as the second passer in the Wolverines’ 2027 class. “Getting to experience The Big House and the fans there, it was a pretty crazy environment to be in,” Hall said. “It was definitely the craziest atmosphere I’ve ever been in.” Through 13 games, Hall has completed 77.6 percent of his passes for 3,253 yards. He threw 51 touchdown passes against just three interceptions and ran for four more scores. Now he gets to play for a state title with his college decision already made. Cass Tech’s Mylan Griggs explains why Michigan is still in the mix Detroit Cass Tech’s Mylan Griggs used the fall to see schools farther from home, including UCLA and Washington. item.title: Pundit tells Arsenal who to sign instead of Calvert-Lewin
item.description: Pundit tells Arsenal who to sign instead of Calvert-Lewin Arsenal have been advised to consider signing Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but pundit Joel Beya believes the Leeds United striker may not be the right choice for the Gunners. He has instead recommended that the club target a younger forward who could offer greater potential for the future. Viktor Gyokeres has not yet met expectations at the Emirates, raising the possibility that Arsenal could return to the transfer market for another striker in one of the next two windows. Several players are reportedly on their radar as they assess how to improve their attacking options. Calvert-Lewin was previously linked with Arsenal during one of the strongest periods of his career at Everton. He has since joined Leeds United and is performing well there, attracting renewed attention from people who believe he could also contribute at a club with greater ambitions. Theo Walcott has urged Arsenal to consider signing the Englishman , believing he could strengthen their forward options. However, Beya is not convinced that pursuing the Leeds striker would be the best decision. Beya questions Calvert-Lewin as an Arsenal target Beya believes Calvert-Lewin could be useful as a backup option, but he does not see him as the ideal signing if Arsenal want to take their attack forward. The pundit feels the club should focus on a younger player who could make a greater contribution over the longer term. Speaking on TalkSport , he explained his position: “I like Calvert-Lewin as a back-up striker, maybe. No disrespect, he’s obviously still doing a good job at Leeds. “I think we should be looking at the Kroupi’s of this world, we should be looking at people that are going to take us forward.” (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) Arsenal urged to consider younger striker Beya’s comments suggest that Arsenal should look beyond players who could provide immediate cover and prioritise a forward with room to develop. His preference is for a younger option who could become an important part of the team’s future. Calvert-Lewin’s current form at Leeds means he remains a possible option, particularly if Arsenal want an experienced striker to provide competition for Gyokeres. However, Beya believes that signing a player with greater long-term potential would be a better approach. Arsenal will have to assess their available options before deciding whether to make another move for a striker. The club’s eventual choice will depend on the qualities they want to add to their attacking department. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Former Arizona pitcher Kevin Ginkel signs with Twins
item.description: Kevin Ginkel during the eighth inning of NLCS Game 7. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Assuming there’s a Major League Baseball season in 2027, which is a big if, Kevin Ginkel will be playing it for a different team than the one with which he’s spent the first decade of his professional career. The former Arizona pitcher has reportedly signed a 2-year deal with the Minnesota Twins. The contract is expected to be worth $18 million, per Jeff Passan of ESPN . The 32-year-old Ginkel finally reached free agency after eight seasons with the Arizona Diamondbacks, the team that drafted him in the 22nd round in 2016. He appeared in 341 MLB games from 2019-26, 3rd-most in franchise history, serving as both a closer and setup man in the bullpen. Ginkel was 6-4 with three saves and a 4.12 ERA in a career-high 74 games in 2026, striking out 72 in 67.2 innings. Since making his MLB debut he’s won 28 games and saved 19 during the regular season, and in the DBacks’ run to the World Series in 2023 he tossed 11.2 scoreless innings over 10 playoff outings. A member of the UA’s College World Series team in 2016, Ginkel spent just one season with the Wildcats after transferring from Southwest College. During the 2016 season he was 5-1 with a 2.80 ERA in 25 games with seven starts. The Twins finished 77-85 last season but have been aggressive in free agency this month. In addition to Ginkel they signed starter Sonny Gray and re-signed catcher Ryan Jeffers .

item.title: Stats and Snaps – 2026 Week 11, Commanders vs Bengals
item.description: The story of the Commanders’ season has been playing up to the level of the best teams in the league and playing down to the level of some of the worst ones. Until Week 9, they have struggled to find ways to win close games. For the second week in a row, the Commanders pulled off a game winning drive after the two minute warning. While it may be too early to pronounce a turnaround to the disappointing 2026 season, fans who have kept hope alive for a return to 2024 form would have recognised the calm determination and surgical precision Jayden Daniels showed as he led the team into field goal range with 39 seconds remaining. Over the past few games, the Commanders’ identity has finally started to come into focus. In addition to a magician at QB, Daronte Jones’ aggressive defense is emerging as a strength. The Bengals rank 4 th in total points. Prior to facing the Commanders, they were averaging 30.9 point per game. The Commanders are one of only three teams to hold them to under 27 points, along with the Jaguars and Texans. That level of defense, and a quarterback who is up to any challenge, can allow them to compete with the best teams in football, if they can just stay out of their own way. Drew Stevens’ 26 yard field goal with time expiring sealed the Commanders’ first back-to-back win since the divisional round of the 2024 playoffs. They need to keep stacking the wins to catch up with the division-leading Giants and keep their playoff-hopes alive. Fortunately, they only need to tie the Giants’ win total to win the division, thanks to the Week 10 win giving them the advantage of the head-to-head tiebreaker. The Commanders only play two opponents with winning records in seven remaining games, while the Giants have yet to run the gauntlet of the 49ers, Seahawks and Lions. Hopefully the Cowboys stay out of the mix. But the Commanders may have the opportunity to settle the matter if Jerry’s boys make it close by the Week 18 rematch. There is still a lot of football left to play. Against the 7-2 Bengals, the Commanders did what they needed to do to keep their season alive. They will need to keep building on the winning formula of aggressive defense, ball control and executing when it matters to get off of life support and hit the post-season with momentum. Fans who still have doubts just need to rewatch the final two minutes of Monday night’s game. To drive that message home, let’s take a look at who stood out – it’s a long list – whose play left room for improvement – shorter list – and where they all lined up in the Commanders’ 22-20 upset of the Cincinnati Bengals in primetime. In cases where advanced stats are scored differently, I have chosen preferred providers (eg. QB pressures – PFF, yards before contact – PFR). item.title: 5 Bills to watch vs. Chiefs
item.description: The Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in the Thanksgiving nightcap this year, and what a game it should be. The 9-1 Bills are the current No. 1 seed in the AFC playoff picture. Thanks to tiebreakers, the 8-2 Chiefs trail the 8-2 Denver Broncos in the AFC West, so Kansas City is currently the No. 5 seed in the conference. However, a win over the Bills would go a long way towards ensuring that the AFC playoffs run through Arrowhead Stadium. The Bills are coming off a sloppy divisional win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The Chiefs, on the other hand, thoroughly thrashed the Arizona Cardinals. Kansas City has won three games in a row; Buffalo has won six consecutive games. Unless there’s a tie, someone is going to take a loss for the first time in a long time this week. If Buffalo wants to emerge with a win over their bitter conference rival, they’ll need some big performances from their key players. While everyone wants to talk about the quarterbacks in this game, we’re intentionally leaving both Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes out of the columns this week. Those two are pretty obvious. There are plenty of other players worthy of mention, though. Here are five Bills to watch in this critical AFC contest. _____________________________________________________________________________ RB James Cook III Regardless of the weather, Cook is a tremendous key to Buffalo’s success. After a slow start on Sunday, Cook extended his streak of scoring at least one touchdown and rushing for at least 75 yards to nine games, which is a new NFL record. He had previously shared the record at eight games with John Rigging and LaDainian Tomlinson. Cook surpassed the 1,000-yard rushing mark for the fourth consecutive season, and he joins two Hall of Fame former Bills in Thurman Thomas and O.J. Simpson as the only players to achieve that feat in franchise history. The sledding won’t be easy against an outstanding Kansas Cigy tush defense that allows just 3.7 yards per carry on the season, but in a game that’s set to feature horrendous weather, finding space and keeping the offense ahead of the sticks will be of the utmost importance. TE Dalton Kincaid It’s something we’ve said ever since the Bills made Kincaid their first-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. When the big tight end is healthy, Josh Allen’s life is much easier. When he doesn’t play, Allen doesn’t have nearly as much space to operate in the passing game. Last week, Allen threw for 304 yards without Kincaid, but it took 45 passing attempts and some ugly possessions to hit that milestone. If Kincaid is healthy, it gives the Bills their full cadre of pass-catchers against an elite defensive unit. Allen’s quarterback rating when targeting Kincaid was 149.2 last season. Since Kincaid joined the club, Allen has a passer rating of 99.9 with Kincaid in the lineup and 91.2 without him. item.title: Patrick Mouratoglou says if he thinks Alexander Zverev really is the best player in the world after ATP Finals loss
item.description: Alexander Zverev will start the 2027 season as the world number one after recording an outstanding campaign this year. Zverev clinched his first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros in early June, taking advantage of a wide-open draw in Paris and seizing one of the biggest opportunities of his life. The German then reached his first Wimbledon final before adding a second major title to his tally by winning the US Open, six years after his near miss at the same tournament against Dominic Thiem. Despite his achievements this season, Zverev has faced criticism, with many claiming he does not deserve to be the world number one due to being winless against Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner in 2026, as well as his poor record versus top ten players. Photo by Dimitar DILKOFF / AFP via Getty Images Patrick Mouratoglou reacts to Carlos Alcaraz’s comments The criticism raged on after Zverev lost to Alcaraz in the final of the ATP Finals, falling in straight sets. After the match, Alcaraz was asked if he felt like the best player in the world, to which he responded: “No, not at all. The number one is Sascha. He really deserves it. Nobody’s going to take that position and the No. 1 away from him.” In a post on LinkedIn , Serena Williams’ former coach, Patrick Mouratoglou, said: “I love the answer. And he’s right. They all do. That’s why they’re so good. Nobody is diminishing anyone here. When you play those guys, you have to feel it inside you, this conviction that you are the best. If you don’t, you cannot win. “We saw it in Turin when Ben Shelton played Alexander Zverev. I don’t think Ben Shelton entered the court thinking, ‘I’m better than this guy’. He couldn’t play his game, and he lost badly. And yet, generally speaking, Ben Shelton is someone who is super, super confident about his ability to beat everybody. The same is true for Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev. “If Carlos Alcaraz had wanted to give the politically correct answer, he would have said: ‘Zverev is number one, he deserves it.’ And Alexander Zverev does deserve it, Carlos Alcaraz knows that. Still, deep inside, he thinks “I’m better than him”. He should think it, since believing it is exactly what allows him to achieve what he’s achieving. “The same goes for Alexander Zverev. When he walked on court against Carlos Alcaraz, I’m sure he was convinced he was going to win. Two-time Grand Slam champion, number one in the world, ready to show he was the better player. Personally, I think Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner are on a different level from anybody. Alexander Zverev believes otherwise, and that belief is a big part of why he is number one in the world. “What I love most about this moment is the honesty. Carlos Alcaraz says what he thinks. He has everything: the game, the attitude, the way to communicate. That’s why he’s such a global superstar. And he chose the truth over the politically correct.” Alcaraz is currently the world number three, but will soon overtake number t

item.title: Mizzou Faces Old School Test Saturday Against Old Rival
item.description: For 89 years, Missouri belonged to a conference defined by a ground and pound style of football where corn-fed physicality reigned supreme. The Big Eight was one of the most geographically and culturally tight-knit conferences in the sport. It was the product of an era where the similarities shared by a group of universities and its fanbases — not how much money they could collectively get in a media rights deal — determined who you played each season. MU gets to relive some of that history Saturday when it hosts old foe Oklahoma, one of the new(er) kids on the block in the SEC and the Tigers’ designated rival at the end of the regular season. For their part, the Sooners are already rekindling some of that Big Eight magic with a late season hot streak spurred by a resurgent run game. Oklahoma’s offense was barely animate for much of the season, a big reason why the squad limped to a 4-4 start despite having an elite defensive unit. But after a resounding loss to South Carolina, head coach Brent Venables finally pulled the plug and replaced offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle with Jason Witten. Three straight wins — including a pair of victories over ranked opponents in Ole Miss and Florida — followed the switch. “They’ve found their identity with coach Witten and their offensive coordinator adjustment,” Drinkwitz said, “He’s really doing a good job; they established the run.” The Sooners are averaging roughly five more points per game under Witten. As Drinkwitz alluded to, much of that improvement can be credited to their ground game. OU averaged just under 105 yards per game and an average of merely 3.09 yards per carry during conference play during its 2-3 start to conference play. Those numbers have jumped to more than 161 yards per game and 3.84 yards per carry under Witten. And much of that improvement can be seen directly in the Sooners’ signal caller. “John Mateer has been an excellent quarterback,” Drinkwitz said, “[He] has played his best ball these last three games.” The former Washington State transfer was mostly a non-factor in the running game for most of the season, collecting about 15 yards per game and 1.3 yards per carry against SEC opponents. But the switch to Witten as the offensive coordinator completely transformed Mateer, who has collected more than 50 yards on the ground in each of his past three games and averaged a far more robust 3.84 yards per carry during that stretch. Mizzou linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez had a simple answer for how to stop Oklahoma’s suddenly potent rushing attack: “Have to have gap integrity and just be physical.” That might be easier said than done, especially for a Tigers squad that has struggled with run defense each of the past two weeks against Georgia and Kentucky. item.title: FCS Playoffs Round 1 Game of the Week: Idaho State Bengals @ North Dakota Hawks: How to Watch, Preview, Predictions
item.description: LOGAN, UT - SEPTEMBER 9: Jordan Cooke #1 of the Idaho State Bengals looks to throw a pass during the first half of their game against the Utah State Aggies at Maverik Stadium September 9, 2023 in Logan, Utah. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Date: Saturday, November 28 Time: 1:00 PM (ET) TV: ESPN+ The Quick Hits It’s playoff time in the FCS and, in a first round chock full of exciting matchups, the best one might be going down in Grand Forks on Saturday afternoon. North Dakota (8-4) nabbed the ninth overall seed in this year’s postseason and they’ll be home for Thanksgiving weekend, hosting Idaho State (7-5). The Hawks made it the second round a season ago and have their sights set much higher this time around. UND has ridden its stifling defense to a first round home game but, even in the comforts of the Alerus Center, might have their hands full with a much-improved ISU team. The Bengals are making their first playoff showing since all the way back in 1983 and to them it has to feel somewhat like a second life. Idaho State was not sure it would even be in the playoffs but got one of the last few spots. With a high-octane offense and strong defense of its own, the cats from Pocatello don’t have any plans of having their season end this weekend. Of course it will for someone, though. It wouldn’t be the playoffs without a Big Sky and Missouri Valley clash and we get a good one right off the jump. The Coaches It’s been a steady build to this moment for Idaho State ever since it hired Cody Hawkins to be its next head coach. Hawkins, son of longtime UC Davis head coach Dan Hawkins, has turned the Bengals around during his four seasons. The team has improved in its win total in each of those years and now he’s taken them as far as they’ve been in decades. Hawkins is a former quarterback and spent his playing days at Colorado from 2006 to 2009. He served as an assistant at Ohio State and UC Davis before eventually making his way over to ISU and, at least right now, it’s safe to say he’s been a home run hire. North Dakota is under the direction of second-year head coach Eric Schmidt. Schmidt took over for Bubba Schweigert following the 2024 season and has gotten UND to the postseason now in each of his two years in charge. With a 16-10 overall record and 10-6 conference mark, Schmidt has been able to maintain the standard of winning. He is a Hawks alum, having played linebacker for the team from 1998 to 2001. Schmidt had the program finish inside the Top 15 of the national rankings last year. North Dakota Offense vs. Idaho State Defense North Dakota’s offense is going to have its work cut out for it against a very talented Idaho State front at it starts with freshman defensive tackle Trehsyn Fesili. Fesili, who was just named a finalist for the Buck Buchanan Award, logged 11.5 tackles for loss and eight sacks this season along with 11 QB hits and five forced fumbles. item.title: Canucks Ice Time: Which Players Does Malhotra Trust Most?
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Vancouver Canucks have a mix of veteran and young talent, which can lead to interesting disparities in ice time. Who does Head Coach Manny Malhotra trust the most to handle the tough minutes? Who is on thin ice? Most Trusted Veterans Malhotra and the Canucks want to win every game. Therefore, the seasoned players are getting a lot of game time. Sometimes, it can border on being too much ice time for some of the veterans. It does say a lot about how much the head coach trusts these players, though. Filip Hronek Filip Hronek is averaging 26:47 of ice time per game, which is fourth in the NHL. He has also played the most cumulative minutes in the league. As the Canucks defensive core has three players 23 and younger, it does make sense that they are being sheltered a bit, which means that Hronek has to do the heavy lifting. Hronek has played over 30 minutes in four games, which is tied for the most in the NHL, with fellow minute-munchers Zach Werenski and Matthew Schaefer . There is a concern that the Canucks are overplaying Hronek and, in the process, not giving younger players enough ice time. However, as younger defenders are still learning the game, there is a balance to be struck. Malhotra clearly trusts Hronek, even though he has had his share of defensive lapses this season. Elias Pettersson (Forward) It is indisputable that Elias Pettersson has been a critical part of this team. He plays in all situations and, for the most part, has been solid this season. His production has been higher, and he has taken the most faceoffs in the NHL. He has averaged 20:42 per game and has played over 20 minutes in 15 out of 24 games. The most prominent part of Pettersson’s game is his work on the penalty kill. Out of the 34 power-play goals the Canucks have surrendered, Pettersson has only been on the ice for eight of them. His two-way game is genuinely impressive, and he has blocked 32 shots this season, by far the most among Canuck forwards. While he still has a ways to go in his offense, Malhotra trusts Pettersson’s two-way capabilities, and without him in the lineup, the defensive zone coverage has been staggeringly poor. Brock Boeser and Filip Chytil Rounding out the forward group is the ice time of Boeser and Chytil, who have recorded an average of 19:38 and 19:21 of ice time this season. I don’t think Boeser’s role on the team has to be reiterated. He is a smart player who can use his hockey IQ to make up for his lack of foot speed. Like the veteran Pettersson, he plays in all situations and will always be a player who closes out competitive games. He is also the undisputed leader of this team . The interesting player to watch is Filip Chytil . Before this season, his highest season-average in ice time was 16:42. What has made Malhotra play Chytil so much more this season? item.title: What Wyndham Clark found ‘shocking’ about the PGA Tour during his rookie year
item.description: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images Wyndham Clark now has six PGA Tour titles to his name after a three-win season in 2026. Clark also added another major to his résumé after triumphing at the US Open at Shinnecock Hills this year. The 32-year-old has reestablished himself as one of the best players in the game this year, after going through real turmoil in 2025, both on and off the golf course. Wyndham Clark seems to be much happier in himself now, and that showed on the golf course throughout the 2026 PGA Tour season. Now that he has been around the block a few times, Clark has shared what some people do not realize about the PGA Tour when watching on their TV screens. What Wyndham Clark found ‘shocking’ about the PGA Tour during his rookie year The two-time major champion made an appearance on The Vanity Index Podcast and was asked what surprised him most about the PGA Tour when he first got his card. “ I would just say probably just the amount of golf you play, “ Clark replied. “ You play in college, you know, you play 11 or 12 events, and then you have your summer events, and it ends up being, you know, 16 to 18 events that you play. “ And then you get to the PGA Tour, and you’re playing 30 weeks because you’ve got to try and keep your card. Then because of how competitive it’s got, you can’t take time off like I was alluding to. “ You know, it’s just not as glamorous as people think. I think when you’re winning, and you’re in the limelight, and winning big tournaments, it’s amazing, but then there’s also just so much of a grind. “ The craziest thing is you play this big tournament, and then the next week, you’ve got another tournament, and it just is this never-ending cycle, and I just thought that was interesting. “ Everyone sees us on TV, like how glamorous it is, and, you know, you see the pretty stuff, but when you’re there on a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and the travel Sunday night, and TSA and bags and all that stuff, it’s like, it’s a grind. I think that is, that was the most shocking. “ The good thing is that once you reach Wyndham Clark’s level, you don’t have to play 30 events anymore. For example, Clark played 25 tournaments on the PGA Tour throughout the 2026 season and that is around 5 more than the biggest names in the game usually play. It will be interesting to see whether he eases up on his schedule in 2027, with the 2028 PGA Tour season expected to be trimmed down to around 20 events.

item.title: Cosmic 'betta fish' glows in spectacular nebula portrait | Space photo of the day for Nov. 26, 2026
item.description: null An image captured by the Dark Energy Camera showcasing the Betta Fish Nebula. (Image credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA) The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape, a stunning wisp of material leftover from a stellar explosion. What is it? Roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth and nestled in the Centaurus constellation, this piece of the supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7 has earned the nickname the Betta Fish Nebula for its floaty, fishy shape. This almost ghostly whirl of gas and dust was created when a star much more massive than our sun exploded, blasting its outer layers of material outward in the process. Over time, the remnants of this supernova eruption stretched outward into space, dispersing and colliding with surrounding gas. The explosive remnants mixing with gas in the interstellar medium created this glowing, blue cloud. This celestial scene was captured by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam), that was created by the U.S. Department of Energy. The camera is installed on the National Science Foundation's Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile. Why is it incredible? This image of a colossal, cosmic "fish" was captured by a camera meant to study the illusive effects of dark energy , which is the name scientists have given for whatever mysterious something is causing the universe to expand at an accelerating rate . The camera is used as part of the Dark Energy Survey, a six-year, international collaboration in which scientists have collected observations of hundreds of millions of galaxies, thousands of supernova and additional details about our cosmos that could help to fill in the picture of the nature of dark energy. And while researchers this past January revealed the initial result of this six-year survey, scientists continue to explore the possibilities of dark energy with DECam alongside instruments like the recently-launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. However, while the survey has lofty goals with its DECam data, the camera can also capture beautiful imagery like this cerulean wisp thousands of light-years away.

item.title: Why Niniola and I have never released a song together – Teni
item.description: Nigerian singer Teni has explained why she and her elder sister, fellow music star Niniola, have yet to release a song together despite their individual successes in the music industry. The singer made the revelation during a question and answer session on Tea with Taylor , hosted by actor Taymesan Emmanuel. Comedian Bovi, who was among the audience, asked Teni why the sisters had never collaborated on a song, prompting her to explain that their conversations rarely revolve around music. According to her, whenever they meet or speak, they spend most of their time chatting and discussing other matters rather than working on music. “We are just two crazy girls. We will just be doing amebo and gisting all the time, forgetting to make music,” she said. She added that music hardly comes up whenever they speak, but suggested that fans could finally get the long-awaited collaboration in 2027. “I kid you not, every time Nini and I talk, we never talk about music. I know it’s bad. We are going to give you guys come 2027,” Teni said. The singer’s comments have renewed anticipation among fans for a joint project from the sisters, whose careers have developed independently within the Nigerian music industry. Teni, whose full name is Teniola Apata, gained prominence with songs such as Uyo Meyo and Case , while Niniola, born Niniola Apata, established herself with popular tracks including Maradona and Bana . Both singers have earned recognition for their distinct musical styles, with Teni known for her playful delivery and Niniola celebrated for her blend of Afro-house and other contemporary African sounds. Although they have not released a joint song, Teni’s latest remarks suggest that a collaboration could be on the way in 2027. The post Why Niniola and I have never released a song together – Teni appeared first on Vanguard News .
