item.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
item.description: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data. In a notice posted on Tuesday , the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data. "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments." Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform. According to a customer notification seen by The Register , the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm. The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes. "With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers. Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post. "An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen." Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage. Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind. Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

item.title: Anambra: Pregnant woman delivers after APLUC seals building
item.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — A nine-month pregnant woman, Mrs Nkechi Theophlus, has delivered her baby after reportedly collapsing following the sealing of her residential building by officials of the Anambra State Property and Land Use Charge (APLUC) in Obosi, Idemili North Local Government Area of the state. The woman reportedly went into labour and delivered her baby in the early hours of Thursday after being rushed to a hospital following the incident. The incident occurred at No. 1 Anyeji Omenwa Street, Obosi, where the officials allegedly padlocked the main entrance to the compound and sealed the building with red tape. The sealing reportedly left the landlady, Prophetess Ukamaka Lauretta Okafor, tenants and other occupants of the three-storey building, comprising 11 flats and rooms in the boys’ quarters, unable to gain access to their homes. The landlady, who protested the action, accused APLUC officials of refusing to issue her a receipt for the N120,000 she allegedly paid to the agency in February, while demanding additional payments. Addressing journalists on Thursday, Okafor said she was not indebted to the agency, insisting that the officials had failed to provide evidence of the full payment she made. She alleged that although N120,000 was deducted from her account through the officials’ Point of Sale (POS) machine, she was issued a receipt for only N90,000. According to her, the officials promised to provide a receipt for the outstanding N30,000 at their office but failed to do so despite her repeated visits. She said she was subsequently informed that the N120,000 payment covered her 2024 liability, while further payments were required for 2025 and 2026. Okafor said she expressed willingness to settle the outstanding payments but insisted that she must first receive evidence of the previous payment. She alleged that the officials refused to issue receipts or a covering note for subsequent payments, instead asking her to pay cash or surrender her ATM card for transactions through their POS machine. She said: “As I am speaking with you now, the N120,000 I paid in February this year, they have not given me the receipt. “I now told them that I will not continue to pay money that won’t be receipted or any evidence of payment given to me. I even told them to give me a covering note for me to pay all the money they are demanding, that I am ready at any moment to pay all the money they are demanding, but they insisted they won’t give me any receipt or covering note.” The landlady also alleged that the enforcement exercise was carried out without prior notice to her or other occupants of the building. She said the sealing left children returning from school and other tenants stranded outside their homes, with some forced to spend the night outdoors. item.title: Full list as CAF shortlist 5 for Women’s Player of the Year award
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has unveiled five finalists for the 2026 Women’s Player of the Year award, with Malawi sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga leading a shortlist featuring some of the continent’s outstanding footballers. Cameroon’s Monique Ngock, Zambia’s Barbra Banda and Morocco’s Hanane Aït El Haj complete the five-player list for African women’s football’s highest individual honour. The finalists were selected from an initial shortlist of 10 nominees based on their performances for club and country during the year. The shortlist reflects an eventful year for women’s football in Africa, highlighted by Cameroon’s historic triumph at the TotalEnergies CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) Morocco 2026 and Malawi’s remarkable run to the final on their tournament debut. The winner will be announced at the CAF Awards 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria, on Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre. The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 7pm Nigerian time. 5 finalists for CAF Women’s Player of the Year 2026 1. Monique Ngock (Cameroon / Washington Spirit) Cameroon’s Monique Ngock earned a place among the finalists following her influential performances in helping the Indomitable Lionesses win their first WAFCON title at the 2026 tournament in Morocco. The midfielder was named Best Player of the Tournament after playing a key role in Cameroon’s historic campaign, which ended with a 3-0 victory over Malawi in the final in Rabat. Her commanding displays, technical ability and leadership in midfield also earned her a place in CAF’s official Team of the Tournament. Her contributions to the national team, alongside her performances for US club Washington Spirit, have strengthened her reputation as one of Africa’s leading midfielders. 2. Temwa Chawinga (Malawi / Kansas City Current) Temwa Chawinga enjoyed an outstanding year, helping Malawi reach the WAFCON 2026 final on their tournament debut and secure historic qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. The forward won the Golden Boot at the tournament after scoring five goals and providing two assists. She finished level on goals with Zambia’s Barbra Banda and Cameroon’s Marie Ngah Manga but claimed the award on the strength of her assists. Temwa’s performances also earned her a place in CAF’s Team of the Tournament. 3. Tabitha Chawinga (Malawi / OL Lyonnes) Tabitha Chawinga joins her younger sister Temwa on the final shortlist after playing an important role in Malawi’s impressive campaign at WAFCON 2026. The OL Lyonnes forward brought experience, creativity and goalscoring quality to the Malawian side as they defied expectations to reach the final. Her performances earned her a place in CAF’s Team of the Tournament, while her achievements in European club football further underline her status among Africa’s leading players. 4. item.title: Ebonyi NDC deputy gov candidate defects to APC; declares support for Tinubu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) deputy governorship candidate in Ebonyi State, Ambassador Uka Chris Ndubuisi, has defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC), declaring support for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Francis Nwifuru. Ndubuisi announced his decision at the APC governorship campaign rally in Ebonyi State on Thursday, saying he had chosen to leave the NDC and collapse the party’s structure in the state. “My name is Ambassador Uka Chris Ndubuisi, and I am the Deputy Governorship candidate of NDC, and also the NDC Youth National Publicity Secretary. “No two ways. I just want to make this declaration that I have decided. Nobody forced me to it; on my own, I have decided to give my support to Mr President Bola Tinubu and our beloved Governor, His Excellency Francis Nwifuru. From today, we are collapsing the structure of NDC in Ebonyi State,” he said. Ndubuisi was received by Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru; Former governor and Minister of Works, David Umahi and APC supporters in the state. Umahi presented him to the party chairman, who was to formally hand him over to Nwifuru, the party’s leader in the state. According to INEC, Ndubuisi was listed as the running mate to NDC governorship candidate Senator Paulinus Igwe Nwagu for the February 6, 2027 election. The ticket was set to challenge incumbent Governor Francis Nwifuru and his deputy, Patricia Obila, who are seeking re-election on the APC platform. item.description: Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, has urged residents to vote for President Bola Tinubu in 2027, saying the president has demonstrated love for the state through projects and deserves overwhelming support in return. Nwifuru said Ebonyi residents should repay Tinubu’s gesture by delivering 100 per cent of their votes to him in the next presidential election. Nwifuru said the state’s political leadership had promised Tinubu 1.3 million votes, expressing confidence that residents would fulfil the pledge. “Our leader said we are promising him 1.3 million votes. I want to tell you, I’m not here to campaign for myself. I am here to campaign for our dear president,” the governor said. He urged the people to acknowledge the projects and interventions the president had brought to Ebonyi, saying the benefits were visible and should not be overlooked. According to him, the Minister of Works had already outlined the projects executed or being undertaken in the state, adding that residents should take the message to their communities. Nwifuru insisted that Tinubu’s commitment to Ebonyi was unmatched, urging residents to demonstrate their appreciation through their votes. “You refused to see what he’s done, and it’s something that is very practical. The Honourable Minister of Works has enumerated it, you’ve heard from him, but I want you to take this message home,” he said. “No other person will love us the way President Bola Ahmed Tinubu loves us, and it’s a payback time,” the governor added. item.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack
item.description: Peninsula Energy has temporarily shut down its Wyoming uranium operation after a "cybersecurity incident" affected plant and wellfield control systems. The Australian uranium producer said on Wednesday that it had activated its response procedures and brought in outside specialists following the attack on its US subsidiary, Strata Energy, which operates the Lance uranium project. Peninsula Energy said it believes the attack is "confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems," and that back-office functions, such as payroll and other corporate systems, in both the US and Australia, remain unaffected. "The company's immediate priorities have been to protect the safety of its employees, secure its operating systems, and work towards the restoration of operations in a safe and controlled manner," it said in an update to the Australian Securities Exchange. The notification [PDF] went on to say that Peninsula Energy's investigations into the attack, including whether any data was compromised, remain ongoing. Peninsula has not given a restart date and says it cannot yet assess the impact on its 2027 production guidance. Operations will remain suspended until recovery and safety checks are complete. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said. The disclosure of additional information came two days after Peninsula secured a short trading halt, which referenced a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming site. The November 23 filing [PDF] dated the incident to Friday evening in Western Australia. Wednesday's update clarified that Strata detected it on the morning of November 20, local US time. Peninsula subsequently requested a voluntary suspension of trading until the earlier of November 30 or an announcement on restarting operations and any resulting change to production guidance. Peninsula's Lance project is a uranium mining operation, extracting the element from underground deposits and turning it into uranium concentrate, aka yellowcake or U₃O₈. Uranium concentrate is feedstock for nuclear fuel production, typically undergoing conversion, enrichment, and fabrication into uranium dioxide pellets before use in reactors. The Lance central processing plant was constructed to produce a maximum of 2.0 million pounds (Mlb) of U₃O₈ annually, and is licensed for 3.0 Mlb. Peninsula previously forecast production of 500,000 to 600,000 pounds in 2027, having withdrawn its 2026 guidance earlier this year following operational problems at Lance. It now says it will reassess the 2027 outlook once operations resume. ®

item.title: Here’s where you can save (a little) on the Ocarina of Time remake
item.description: The Nintendo Switch 2 remake delivers a complete graphical overhaul and numerous quality-of-life updates to the ‘98 classic. | Image: Nintendo A lot of people have The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2 on their holiday wishlist. In case you haven’t bought it yet, I wanted to share some small but welcome deals happening on the physical and digital versions of the game. Costco members can currently grab the cartridge edition for $62.99, down from its regular price of $69.99 (it’s the only retailer currently discounting the physical version). Both Amazon and Costco are also selling the digital version for $54.99, a small $5 discount. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Where to Buy: $59.99 $54.99 at Amazon (Digital) $69.99 $62.99 at Costco (Physical) Ocarina of Time is one of Nintendo’s most groundbreaking titles, having served as its first 3D Zelda game when it launched in 1998. Parts of the original game haven’t aged particularly well — namely some dungeon design and the game’s tricky 3D navigation, since there was only one analog stick at the time — which makes it tough for some to enjoy going back to play the N64 version. Thankfully, the Switch 2 remake introduces several fixes, a host of quality-of-life improvements, and, of course, some lovely visuals that make it a graphics powerhouse by today’s standards. If you go the digital route, a recent Switch 2 update lets you gift games to players in your family group. It doesn’t have to be your actual family, either, just up to eight people you designate as part of your group. The digital game will then appear gift-wrapped on their homescreen. Read our full Ocarina of Time review .

item.title: 74 Killed In Niger Communal Clash, Bago Orders Investigation, Donates N148m To Families
item.description: The clash between Kambari vigilantes and Fulani herders in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State resulted in the death of 74 persons. The state’s governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, disclosed this during a visit to the Emir of Borgu, Alhaji Halilu Sani Dantoro, at his palace in New Bussa, the LGA’s headquarters. Terrorists had, last Saturday, attacked Lumman-Ba’are community in Borgu LGA, killing the village head, Mallam Bawa Muhammad, his wife and three of his children. They also set his palace ablaze. Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, has ordered a thorough investigation into the clashes.‎ ‎The governor commiserated with the traditional ruler and people of the kingdom over the tragic incident. ‎Bago said the investigation was aimed at identifying those responsible for the violence and uncovering the remote and immediate causes of the recurring communal conflicts, with a view to preventing future occurrences. ‎He called on residents of the affected communities to embrace peaceful coexistence, tolerance and mutual understanding, stressing that no meaningful development could take place in an atmosphere of violence and hostility. ‎The governor expressed sympathy with the families of the victims and announced a donation of ₦2 million to each of the 74 affected families, amounting to ₦148 million, alongside the provision of foodstuffs and building materials to support those whose houses were destroyed during the clashes. ‎He commended the Borgu Emirate Council for its continued efforts towards maintaining peace and unity among the people, while urging Nigerians to learn to live together irrespective of their differences. ‎In his response, the Emir of Borgu, Muhammad Haliru -Dantoro Kitoro IV, appreciated the governor for the condolence visit and the timely deployment of security personnel to the area. ‎The traditional ruler acknowledged the state government’s efforts in deploying joint tactical security teams to tackle security challenges, including insurgency, in the area. He, however, expressed sadness that some individuals had chosen to resort to violence despite ongoing efforts by the government and security agencies to restore lasting peace. ‎The Emir also commended security agencies for their swift response, which he said helped to contain the situation and restore normalcy to the affected communities. ‎In his remarks, the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi, commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his efforts towards addressing security challenges across the country, noting that the restructuring of the nation’s security architecture was yielding positive results. ‎He also praised Governor Bago for his commitment to tackling insecurity in parts of Niger State and acknowledged the contributions of security agencies in containing threats to lives and property. ‎The governor was accompanied on the visit by the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi; Member representing Borgu/Agwara Federal Cons

item.title: FG issues strong advisory on harmattan fires, flags off safety campaign
item.description: …Warns against attacks on firefighters, careless fuel storage By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has issued a strong advisory on the risk of fire during the harmattan season, urging Nigerians to avoid overloading electrical sockets, leaving cooking unattended, burning refuse indiscriminately and storing petrol carelessly. The Controller General of the Federal Fire Service FFS, Samuel Adeyemi Olumode, gave the advisory on Thursday while flagging off the 2026 Harmattan Fire Safety Campaign. The campaign will run through February 2027. He spoke via a virtual fire chat on “The Roles and Responsibilities of Stakeholders in Building a Fire Safety-Resilient Community.” “The Harmattan period comes with dry and dusty weather conditions, low humidity and dry vegetation, all of which can contribute to the rapid spread of fire. “Activities involving cooking, electrical appliances, generators, gas cylinders, fuel storage and open burning require greater caution during this period”, he said. He advised households to “regularly inspect gas cylinders, hoses and connections, and ensure that generators are operated in properly ventilated outdoor spaces.” Parents and guardians, he said, “must also keep matches, lighters and other ignition sources away from children.” Olumode also warned business owners, market operators, school administrators, event organisers and managers of public facilities to put proper fire safety arrangements in place. “Prevention should never be treated as an expense that can be postponed until an emergency occurs,” he said. The Controller General condemned a recent attack on firefighters who were attacked at 7th Avenue, Gwarinpa, Abuja, on Friday, 13th November 2026. “At about 10am, firefighters from the Kubwa Metropolitan Fire Station, who had responded to a distress call, were attacked by suspected hoodlums who pelted them with stones. One of our personnel sustained a head injury and required medical attention. “Let me state clearly that attacks on firefighters will not be tolerated,” Olumode declared, adding that the suspected perpetrators had been apprehended. “Let me assure Nigerians that this matter will not be treated lightly. The appropriate authorities will ensure that those found culpable face the full weight of the law. There must be no justification for violence against emergency responders”, he said. The CGF said no emergency response system could function effectively “when firefighters are attacked, obstructed or prevented from carrying out their duties.” Olumode linked the safety of responders to the Service’s 15-minute response-time target. Meeting it, he said, “requires properly located fire stations, accessible roads, prompt reporting of incidents, cooperation from residents and an environment in which firefighters can perform their duties without obstruction or intimidation.” On the Service’s performance, he said between January and June 2026 it “responded to 491 fire incidents, saved 1,725 lives and protected

item.title: WhatsApp to allow users schedule messages – here’s how you can
item.description: WhatsApp has introduced a scheduled messaging feature that allows users to compose messages in advance and choose when they should be delivered, addressing one of the most requested additions to the messaging platform. The feature will enable users to schedule messages between 10 minutes and 14 days ahead in both individual and group chats. Announcing the update, WhatsApp said the feature would allow users to write messages when they think of them and have them delivered at a more appropriate time. “That’s why we’re introducing scheduled messages – one of our most requested features. You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats,” the company said. According to WhatsApp, scheduled messages will appear in recipients’ chats like ordinary messages, without any indication that they were composed and scheduled earlier. Users will also be able to view all their scheduled messages and delete them before delivery if they change their minds. How to schedule messages on WhatsApp To schedule a message on WhatsApp, users can follow these steps: Open WhatsApp and select an individual or group chat. Type the message they want to send. Press and hold the send button. Select the preferred date and time for the message to be delivered. Confirm the schedule. The message will then be delivered automatically at the selected time. WhatsApp said scheduled messages would still be delivered even if the sender’s phone was switched off or ran out of battery. The feature will support text messages, photographs and videos, giving users the option to plan different types of communication ahead of time. The company also assured users that scheduled messages would retain WhatsApp’s end-to-end encryption, meaning only the sender and intended recipients would be able to read them. “Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us,” WhatsApp said. The scheduled messaging feature is rolling out globally over the coming weeks, although the company did not specify when it would become available to all users. WhatsApp said the update was another way for users to stay connected with important people by ensuring their messages arrive at exactly the right time. item.title: Nigeria’s trade hits ₦41.4tn in Q2 as NPA records 24.8% cargo growth
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Nigeria’s expanding trade activities are increasingly highlighting the strategic importance of the maritime sector, with cargo volumes handled across the nation’s seaports recording significant growth amid rising merchandise trade. The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) disclosed that cargo throughput across Nigerian ports rose by 24.8 per cent, from 103.6 million metric tonnes in 2024 to 129.3 million metric tonnes in 2025, indicating increased port utilisation and growing cargo-handling activities. The growth momentum extended into the first half of 2026, as cargo throughput increased by 12.2 per cent to 68.2 million metric tonnes, compared with 60.8 million metric tonnes recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The development comes against the backdrop of Nigeria’s merchandise trade rising to ₦41.4 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, further highlighting the critical role of ports in facilitating international trade, cargo movement and broader economic activities. Speaking at a two-day data-driven business and maritime reporting training organised in partnership with the Premium Times Training Academy in Ikeja, Lagos, on Wednesday, the General Manager, Corporate Affairs Division, NPA, Mr Ikechukwu Onyemekara, urged journalists to embrace evidence-based journalism, saying accurate maritime reporting was critical to trade, investment decisions and public understanding of the economy. He said Nigeria’s merchandise trade value of ₦41.4 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, representing a 5.6 per cent increase over the corresponding period of 2025, demonstrated the scale of economic activity linked to the movement of cargo through the country’s ports. According to him, port efficiency has far-reaching implications for manufacturers, exporters, importers, consumers and investors, as delays and operational bottlenecks ultimately increase the cost of doing business and affect the prices of goods. Onyemekara said the country’s ports received 2,300 ships in the first half of 2026, compared with 2,152 vessels in the same period of 2025, while outward cargo accounted for 41.9 per cent of total throughput in the second quarter, indicating improved export activity. He urged maritime journalists to look beyond headline figures and examine the factors driving growth, citing Lekki Deep Sea Port, which handled nearly 40 per cent of cargo throughput across Nigerian ports in the first half of 2026. He said more than three-quarters of Lekki’s cargo traffic was linked to refinery operations, stressing that a breakdown of the figures was necessary to understand how industrial investments were reshaping port activities and trade flows. On the NPA’s reform efforts, Onyemekara said the authority was pursuing port modernisation, digitalisation, export facilitation and sustainability initiatives to improve efficiency and competitiveness. item.title: Housing crisis on the ballot: Anger boils over ahead of Spanish election
item.description: Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday in a general election that was called after street protests for affordable housing. Anger bubbled over after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her home of seven decades and two decrees to tackle the housing crisis were rejected by parliament. In calling the snap election, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is hoping the housing issue can galvanise his left-wing base.

item.description: “The implications of having the far right in power in Brussels are enormous,” warns Sophie Pornschlegel, Senior Advisor at the European Policy Centre. With elections approaching in several EU member states, including France and Italy, what would a growing number of far-right, Eurosceptic governments mean for the EU budget, relations between European institutions, common legislation and support for Ukraine? Could Giorgia Meloni could adopt a more radical stance? “The whole idea of the EU is to have a common legislation that is then applied in 27 member states. Otherwise, what is the point of having the EU?”

item.title: Plateau Attack: Death toll rises to 19
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The death toll from an attack on Tafi-Gana (Cando Zrreci), a community in Jebbu Miango, Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, has risen to 19 following the death of three persons who were rushed to hospital after the incident. The attack reportedly occurred on Wednesday night, November 25, and continued into the early hours of Thursday, November 26, 2026, throwing the community into confusion, fear and panic. A resident of the community, Moses Monday, who confirmed the casualty figure on Thursday, said 16 bodies were recovered at the scene, while three other victims died after being taken to hospital. Monday said: “This is evil. I can confirm that 16 bodies have so far been recovered at the spot, with an additional three who died after they were taken to the hospital. These evil men will not rest.” Another resident, Nuhu Fidelis, who also confirmed the attack, described it as another assault on a neighbouring community in Jebbu Miango. Fidelis said: “Yes, in the early morning of today, Thursday. Last night, November 25, 2026, a Christian neighbouring village, Tafi-Gana (Cando Zrreci), in Jebbu Miango, Bassa LGA, Plateau State, was attacked again. Many innocent people lost their lives.” He condemned the killings and called on the government and security agencies to take urgent measures to protect residents. Another resident, Paul Nehemiah, who said he lost a close relative in the attack, described the killings as wicked and unprovoked, adding that residents had been living in fear following repeated attacks. Nehemiah said: “We are tired of burying our people. These are farmers, women and children who did nothing to anyone. How long will this continue? We are calling on the government to rise up and save us.” Rita Joseph, whose family fled the village during the attack, said community members could no longer sleep peacefully because of persistent security threats. She said: “We ran into the bush with our children.” The residents appealed to the Plateau State Government, the Federal Government and security agencies to deploy more personnel to Miango and surrounding communities to prevent further attacks. They also urged the authorities to take decisive action to bring the perpetrators to justice and restore confidence among residents. Efforts to obtain comments from the Plateau State Police Command spokesman, SP Alfred Alabo, and his counterpart at Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, were unsuccessful, as they had yet to respond to inquiries by our correspondent as of the time of filing this report. The post Plateau Attack: Death toll rises to 19 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations
item.description: ‎Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago, has received the report of the Judicial Commission of Inquiry established to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths of 37 artisanal miners while in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Niger State Command. ‎The Governor received the report from the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, at the Government House, Minna, where he reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to implementing its recommendations. ‎Governor Bago expressed appreciation to the Commission on behalf of the bereaved families, the Miners Association and the NSCDC, describing the report as an important document that would guide stakeholders in addressing the circumstances surrounding the tragic incident. ‎He commended Justice Muhammad and members of the Commission for their dedication, sacrifices and thoroughness throughout the investigation, assuring that the government would carefully consider the findings and recommendations. ‎The Governor also disclosed that a copy of the report would be forwarded to the Presidency for reference, underscoring the importance of the investigation and its outcome. ‎Earlier, the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, thanked the Governor for the confidence reposed in the panel and the opportunity to serve. ‎He explained that the Commission received nine memoranda, conducted public hearings and carried out inspection visits to two mining sites, two NSCDC offices and the General Hospital in Minna as part of its investigation. ‎Justice Muhammad said the evidence and facts gathered during the proceedings formed the basis of the Commission’s findings and recommendations. ‎He further explained that the report was presented in three volumes for ease of reference, with Volume One containing the findings, observations and recommendations; Volume Two containing the records of proceedings; and Volume Three comprising all exhibits tendered before the Commission. ‎In his remarks, the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Nasiru Mu’azu, described the deaths of the 37 artisanal miners as a grave incident in the history of Niger State. ‎He commended Governor Bago for demonstrating commitment to the rule of law by establishing the Judicial Commission of Inquiry to investigate the incident and ensure that the circumstances surrounding the deaths were thoroughly examined. ‎Mu’azu assured that the Ministry of Justice would carefully study the report and advise the government on appropriate actions and the next steps to be taken. ‎ ‎ The post Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Company was religious about backups but sinned by leaving them exposed
item.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we’re thankful every time someone leaves a password sticky note on a monitor or fails to delete a terminated employee’s admin account. But neither of those common occurrences is what we’ll be talking about today. Instead, our subject broke the number-one rule of backups: you gotta keep ’em separated. Our story comes courtesy of Da Li, who serves as global alliance manager at Info2Soft , a company that provides data protection and recovery software. At one point, a partner called him into a case where a Chinese vehicle parts manufacturer fell victim to a ransomware gang. Unfortunately, its backup was compromised too. The manufacturer had religiously backed up its manufacturing execution system (MES) and SAP orders, inventory, and finance systems every night. There was even a green dashboard that showed the backup process had succeeded, and someone checked that every morning. However, one Friday evening, crims broke into the network and found out that the backup server was joined to the same Windows domain as the rest of the network. The hackers found a plaintext password for the backup service account in a maintenance script on a file share and discovered that someone had used the very same password for a domain admin account. So the first thing the crooks did was delete every restore point on that backup server. Then they started encrypting the production servers to ransom them. “Every backup job had succeeded for three years,” Li said. “The failure was that the thing meant to save them could be reached with the same keys as the thing being attacked.” The results were devastating. With the MES and SAP data both gone, the plant couldn't schedule production, ship parts, or track them. By the time Li was called in, the plant had already resolved its ransomware situation. We don’t know whether it paid or not. The manufacturer did ask Li and his company to make sure that this couldn’t happen again. Li’s fix was not radical, but it was instructive. He made sure that the company now keeps its backup system outside the production domain, uses unique credentials, and requires MFA to reduce the risk of unauthorized access even if a password is compromised. He also made sure that the company keeps at least one offline backup and runs a test restore quarterly to ensure it’s prepared for emergencies.®

item.title: Tinubu housing projects deliver over 26,000 units, 525,100 jobs, APC-PCC says
item.description: …As MOFI implements N1 trillion mortgage programme By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC said on Thursday thst the President Bola Tinubu administration has facilitated the financing and delivery of over 26,000 housing units and generated 525,100 real estate construction jobs nationwide in the past three years. Spokesperson of the council, Dele Alake, made the claim in a statement issued in Abuja. According to the statement, the Ministry of Finance Incorporated MOFI, through the MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF), has provided more than N158 billion in mortgage financing to 2,269 homebuyers as of October 31, 2026. The statement said the fund financed properties valued at more than N279 billion, while 695 housing units have received offtake guarantees, “creating a ready market for private-sector property development”. It said 6,620 properties have been listed on the fund’s platform, with 21 financial institutions providing mortgage services across 28 states and all six geopolitical zones. MREIF, a N1 trillion housing finance programme sponsored by MOFI, commenced operations on March 17, 2025, to expand access to affordable mortgages and mobilise private investment in the housing sector. The statement said beneficiaries can access mortgage loans at an interest rate of 9.75 per cent per annum, with repayment periods of up to 20 years and a minimum equity contribution of 10 per cent. It added that the fund raised an initial N250 billion, made up of N150 billion in concessionary Federal Government funding and N100 billion in private commercial investment. “To enable more Nigerians to own homes, President Tinubu’s administration recognises that affordable mortgage loans, reasonably priced developer financing, and local production of building materials are crucial to reducing housing costs and expanding construction activities,” the statement said. On construction, the council said the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development is building 10,328 housing units at different stages of completion under the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme. These include 2,744 units at the Renewed Hope City in Abuja, 2,000 in Kano and 2,084 in Lagos, while another 3,500 units are being developed under the Renewed Hope Estates Programme across 14 states. The Federal Housing Authority FHA, it said, is delivering 3,341 units, including 1,550 units for armed forces personnel in Jabi, Abuja. The Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria FMBN accounts for another 11,294 housing units, comprising 9,076 units financed between 2024 and 2025 and 2,218 units delivered in the first quarter of 2026. According to the statement, the ministry’s housing projects are estimated to have generated 258,200 employment opportunities, while FMBN’s interventions have generated 226,900. item.title: FIFA confirms cyberattack, says hackers stole personal, business data
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA has confirmed a criminal cyberattack that exposed a limited amount of personal and business information, while files linked to its abandoned World Cup stake-sale plan were not accessed. According to Reuters, a person with direct knowledge of the incident said less than 0.1 per cent of FIFA’s total data was affected and no files from the FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed. “FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information,” a FIFA spokesperson told Reuters. The football governing body condemned the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data, calling it “a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy”. FIFA did not disclose when the attack took place, how many people or organisations were affected, or what business information was accessed. It also did not say whether any data had appeared online or where it may have been published. FIFA scrapped plans in July to sell private investors a stake in a new unit that would manage its events, including the World Cup. The proposal aimed to raise up to $4.2 billion by selling a 20 per cent stake. The post FIFA confirms cyberattack, says hackers stole personal, business data appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
item.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. item.title: Meet Nigeria’s Damilola Bolarinde, crowned Miss International Africa 2026
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian beauty queen Damilola Bolarinde has been crowned Miss International Africa 2026 after representing the country at the 64th edition of the Miss International pageant in Tokyo, Japan. The continental title was announced on Thursday, November 26, a day after the grand finale held on November 25, which featured 73 contestants from different countries. Bolarinde, popularly known as Queen Dammy, secured a place among the Top 20 contestants but did not advance to the Top 10. Her performance at the competition earned her the Miss International Africa title. The achievement adds to her growing profile in the Nigerian beauty pageant industry, having represented Lagos State at the 2025 Miss Universe Nigeria competition, where she emerged first runner-up behind Anambra State representative, Onyinyechi Basil. In April 2026, Bolarinde won the Face of Hope pageant, earning the right to represent Nigeria at the Miss International competition as Miss International Nigeria 2026. She defeated contestants representing Anambra and Rivers states, who finished as first and second runners-up, respectively, at the event held on April 19 at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos. Meanwhile, Elizaveta Kuznetsova of Moldova won the overall Miss International 2026 crown, becoming the first contestant from her country to claim the title. Brittany Feeney of the United Kingdom finished as first runner-up, while Laura Glozarová of the Czech Republic came third. Victoria Kosasieputri of Indonesia and Khánh Như Lê of Vietnam completed the Top Five, finishing fourth and fifth, respectively. Bolarinde’s continental recognition marks another milestone in her pageant career and adds Nigeria to the list of countries represented among the award recipients at the international competition. The post Meet Nigeria’s Damilola Bolarinde, crowned Miss International Africa 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Stale links on UK public sector websites direct visitors to gambling dens
item.description: UK public sector websites are directing visitors to gambling promotions through old links to defunct local enterprise partnerships (LEPs), research by digital consultancy Digital Royalty has found. The consultancy identified 93 links across 79 pages on websites belonging to 26 public bodies. LEPs brought together councils and businesses to promote economic growth in England under a coalition government initiative launched in 2010. Central government funding ended in April 2024, with their core functions transferred to local and combined authorities. Among other things, Digital Royalty builds and looks after websites, which means chasing down old links. In August, it found that a link on Surrey County Council's website led to a former LEP address now displaying casino content. It went looking for more. Digital Royalty founder Alex De Sousa said: "Slow is usually a sign of caution and diligence, but 31 months after the LEPs wound up, it's crossed into inefficient and dangerous." The consultancy offered The Register four examples of websites run by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS), Hull City Council, Parliament, and the Local Government Association. One example is a government page about the Digital Skills Partnership, originally published under an earlier incarnation of DCMS. The page includes a link that appears to be for the Humber Digital Skills Partnership within the Humber LEP website, but in fact takes users to a site advertising "Independent Non GamStop Casinos UK – New Casino Sites Outside GamStop." GamStop is the self-exclusion scheme designed to help people restrict their online gambling, which makes the links more concerning than ordinary website clutter. The same link appears on the Hull City Council website under a list of Joint Committees, Partnerships and Trusts where it appears as Local Economic Partnership (Humber LEP). An old page for the Parliament website detailing the Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy committee's Industrial Strategy report includes a footnote (135) that appears to be for the Business Central funding finder service, but takes the user to the "Highest RTP Non GamStop Casinos for UK Players." The Local Government Association's (LGA) sustainability and waste route map included a link to the former York and North Yorkshire LEP website. The destination initially appeared legitimate but contained links promoting crypto casinos. The LGA now appears to have removed the link. All the organizations mentioned have been contacted by The Register to offer them the opportunity to comment. Digital Royalty checked former web addresses associated with about 70 LEPs and growth hubs, then used a backlink index to identify roughly 3,000 incoming links from public sector sites. Most were simply outdated rather than leading to gambling content. item.title: Opposition coalition confirms Monday summit, to adopt 3 key documents
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Coalition for Democracy has confirmed that the Second Summit of Nigeria’s opposition political parties will hold on Monday in Abuja, with participating parties expected to adopt three foundational documents. The coalition is a multiparty platform pioneered by the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP). In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties, it said the decision was reached on Wednesday night at the seventh meeting of its Central Leadership Committee. The statement said the leaders reached the decision “following extensive deliberations on the state of the nation, the prevailing political environment and the earlier resolution to suspend campaign activities on day of the Summit”. The leaders, however, made it clear that the suspension does not end inter-party engagement. “The leaders agreed that the suspension of campaign activities does not preclude the continuation of consultations and engagements among opposition political parties on matters of common interest, including electoral integrity, democratic participation and institutional reform,” the statement said. The documents to be considered and adopted are the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity and the National Reform Programme. They were developed by working groups made up of representatives of the constituent parties after the inaugural summit of August 31, 2026. According to the statement, “the documents set out proposed mechanisms for inter-party cooperation and a framework for addressing national governance challenges.” The coalition leaders also reaffirmed their commitment “to working collectively to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process and protect the sanctity of the ballot across the country”. The coalition invited other opposition political parties to participate in the summit and “contribute to the ongoing consultations”. Three personalities will address the summit on the theme, “The Doctrine of a Necessary Democratic Opposition”. They are the Alaago of Kajola Alago, Ileshan, HRH Oba Oladipo Olaitan; Prof. Ango Abdullahi; and Chief S. N. Okeke. The statement said the summit is expected to bring together “national leaders of opposition political parties, elected representatives, former public officeholders, civil society leaders, representatives of the media, and observers from foreign diplomatic missions in Nigeria”. The post Opposition coalition confirms Monday summit, to adopt 3 key documents appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Thanksgiving night sky 2026 — What to look for after dinner tonight
item.description: null If your household is like most American families, then on Thursday you likely will all be sitting down with family and friends for a traditional Thanksgiving turkey dinner during the mid-to-late afternoon hours. Then as darkness falls, some will probably migrate into the living room to catch some football or other holiday fare on television. But if you have a large gathering of family and friends at your home — and if your skies are mainly clear — why not invite everyone outside to gaze at the evening sky? If you have binoculars, or better yet, a telescope, you just might end up turning this into a memorable family tradition of its own. First, the "Lord of the Rings" . . . If I may paraphrase the mysterious voice from the 1989 movie, "Field of Dreams": "If you set up your telescope, they will come." And you'll get a big kick out of your Turkey Day guests uttering all the "oohs" and "ahs" or exclamations of "Wow!" with just one peek through the eyepiece. As darkness falls, Saturn will glow at first magnitude, shining with a sedate, yellow-white light and appearing noticeably brighter than the star Fomalhaut, about 40 degrees (the equivalent of four fist-widths) to its lower right. Its famous ring system is now tilted only about six degrees toward Earth but may be visible with steadied (or image-stabilized) high-power binoculars or through the eyepiece of a telescope magnifying over 30-power. The rings will seem to glow with an inner light and for those who have never had the pleasure of seeing them for themselves, that first view always elicits astonishment; kids especially most often will say: "Awesome!" or "No way!" I've even had people accuse me of using a slide of Saturn, to which I, of course, reply with, "No . . . that's the real thing." Saturn will shine high in the southern sky on Nov. 26. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) . . . and later, the moon Then, along about 6:25 p.m. local time, the waning gibbous moon, 2½ days past full phase and 91% illuminated, will begin to emerge from beyond the east-northeast horizon. Give it another hour and it will stand about 10 degrees above the horizon — equal to the width of your clenched fist held at arm's length. By then, the moon will be in a better position for evening study. Location of the moon at approximately 9p.m. on Thanksgiving. Local moonrise and moonset times will vary depending on your location. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8 ) Even in binoculars, the moon is a striking sight to see. It's such a special object because it doesn't matter whether you live in a rural area or in the middle of a brightly lit city, for the moon can always be readily observed. It always looks spectacular whether you're using binoculars or a telescope. It never looks precisely the same no matter how often you view it and can be observed even on hazy or partially cloud-covered nights. item.title: Remembering Pete Edochie: 5 Films That Made Him a Nollywood Legend
item.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Did you grow up watching Pete Edochie in Nollywood films? Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . Pete Edochie and Genevieve Nnaji behind the scenes on the set of the 2018 film Lionheart, where they played father and daughter Chief Ernest Obiagu and Adaeze Obiagu. Survived by his wife, Josephine, and their six children, including actors Linc and Yul Edochie , he leaves behind a remarkable body of work. As we remember his life and contribution to Nigerian cinema, here are five films that capture some of the performances that made Pete Edochie a household name. Things Fall Apart (1987) Before Nollywood’s home-video boom even began, Pete Edochie became a household name across Nigeria and internationally through his breakout role as Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s classic novel Things Fall Apart. Directed by David Orere , the acclaimed television miniseries marked Edochie’s first professional acting role and saw him bring the proud, fierce, and deeply conflicted Umuofia warrior to life with remarkable nuance. His performance was so transformative that, for generations of viewers, Edochie and Okonkwo became inseparable. Rituals (1997) As Nollywood entered its golden home-video era in the late 1990s, Edochie starred in Andy Amenechi’s gripping thriller Rituals as Don Pedro, a calculating member of a secretive and ruthless society. item.title: 19 years after, Olajumoke’s hostels for disabled students decay
item.description: — Invaded by bedbugs, broken doors, faulty drains — Students seek urgent intervention as AAUA VC promises action By Dayo Johnson AKURE — Nineteen years after former Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, Senator Bode Olajumoke, donated two hostels for students with disabilities, the facilities have fallen into a state of disrepair, with residents appealing to the university authorities for urgent intervention. Olajumoke, who visited the male and female hostels he donated in February 2006, expressed dismay at their condition, describing the facilities as horrible and neglected. Conducted round the buildings by the hostel manager, Joseph Aladegbola, the former senator said the living conditions of the students were unacceptable and urged the university management to urgently rehabilitate the facilities. Olajumoke donated the hostels after discovering that the institution had no accommodation specifically designed for students with disabilities. The two buildings, alongside an office for the hostel manager, were commissioned by former Senate President, Senator Ken Nnamani, with the late Governor Olusegun Agagu as guest of honour. They were purpose-built to accommodate students with physical disabilities, with wide doors and toilets and bathrooms designed to allow wheelchair access. However, the hostel manager attributed the poor state of the facilities to inadequate funding, saying the hostels received maintenance funds at most twice a year, an allocation he described as insufficient to address their needs. After inspecting the buildings, Olajumoke visited the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Tomola Obamuyi, where he raised concerns about the level of deterioration. He warned that the unhygienic conditions could trigger disease outbreaks if urgent steps were not taken to address them. Olajumoke said the male hostel was in a worse condition, adding that both buildings had been invaded by bedbugs and required immediate fumigation. He called on stakeholders to work together to improve the living conditions of students with disabilities. One of the students lamented that the rooms, bathrooms, toilets and kitchen were all in a state of neglect. “The institution has neglected the hostels, the toilets are bad, doors and windows falling, all other facilities are in deplorable conditions,” the student said. The student appealed to the university authorities to restore the buildings to the condition they were in when Olajumoke donated them. Also speaking, a former hall chairman, Joseph Agada, urged the university management to prioritise the renovation of the hostels before the situation deteriorated further. Agada called for comprehensive repairs, including the replacement of damaged bathroom and toilet facilities, provision of new chairs and fumigation to tackle the bedbug infestation. “We need the complete renovation of the two hostels, new chairs, the fumigation of the hostels because of the invasion of bedbugs. item.title: Microsoft hotpatches hotpatch that could crash Windows Server 2025
item.description: Microsoft has released an out-of-band hotpatch to fix a bug in November's Windows Server 2025 security update that could crash some servers when an IPv6 route expires. The patch for the patch, KB5138318 , addresses crashes on systems with Router Advertisement (RA) enabled that receive time-bound IPv6 routes. When a route timer expires, affected servers can halt with error 0x139 (KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE). Issued on November 25, the corrective update takes effect without requiring a restart, according to Microsoft. KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE means the kernel has detected corruption of a critical data structure and stopped the system. Microsoft has identified route-timer expiry as the trigger but hasn't explained the underlying coding fault. Good to see the operating system being protected against the impact of the corruption. Less good for administrators wondering why their servers have suddenly misbehaved. Lansweeper puts Windows Server 2025 at 7 percent of the servers it monitors, compared with 32 percent for Server 2022 and 33 percent for Server 2019. Only systems with the affected hotpatch and networking configuration are implicated. Microsoft's Windows Server updates have not gone well over the last few months, with out-of-band updates issued in September, October, and November. An out-of-band update to deal with a problem introduced in a hotpatch (in this case, KB5131077 ) therefore carries with it a certain sense of inevitability. Hotpatches are a way of getting OS security updates on a Windows Server without requiring a restart and so are, in theory, a boon for administrators keen on maximizing uptime. According to Microsoft, in addition to faster installations and better protection, there is "lower workload impact with less need to restart your machine." Avoiding a planned restart is less of a selling point when the alternative is an unplanned crash. ®

item.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
item.description: Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO 2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it. A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note. Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don't digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO 2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO 2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO 2 . That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane. Read full article Comments

item.title: UK government working 'around the clock' on Capita contingency plans
item.description: The UK government is working "around the clock" on contingency plans for Capita contracts after the outsourcer's CEO quit and its shares plunged, a Cabinet Office minister told MPs. Capita announced plans this week to raise around £190 million through a share issue in the first half of 2027 after warning of sharply lower profits and further costs linked to its Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS) contract. The outsourcer "should be absolutely ashamed of its performance" on the £239 million contract , Sally Jameson, parliamentary secretary in the Cabinet Office, told MPs on Tuesday . "We have seen evidence that it has stepped up in recent months and begun to rectify the problem, but it is inexcusable that it let the situation get to this point," she said. Adolfo Hernandez stepped down as CEO with immediate effect on Monday, with finance chief Pablo Andres taking over. Shares fell around 70 percent following the announcement. In the House of Commons, Jameson was asked about the government's plans if Capita were unable to carry out the remainder of its contract given the outsourcer's performance on the CSPS. "On contingency planning, it is important that we stabilize the situation and that Capita can continue to deliver the pension scheme. However, the government is working across departments, as we do in relation to all strategic suppliers, to ensure that the relevant contingency plans are in place. People are working around the clock on that," she said. Jameson said contingency planning for the pension scheme was already underway before Monday's announcement, describing it as standard practice for major government suppliers. She told the Chamber that the Cabinet Office was "currently arranging to meet the new CEO in the coming days" following Hernandez's departure. The Register first exposed problems with Capita's CSPS portal last December. The site, serving 1.5 million current and former public servants, rejected login details even for newly created accounts, contained broken and circular links, and displayed dummy text. In January this year, the Cabinet Office was forced to promise "interim support measures" for the CSPS following Capita's botched takeover, including 150 additional government staff to clear the backlog in cases. Speaking in Parliament, Conservative MP Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, chair of the Public Accounts Committee, said there had been "some tragic and dreadful cases" since Capita took over administration last December. "I heard of one poor lady who was living on benefits because she could not get the bereavement payments she needed after her sister's death. I have heard of a member of parliamentary staff, not far from this Chamber, who is having to delay his retirement by a year because he cannot even get a statement from the scheme." The government has withheld nearly £10 million in contractual payments over Capita's performance. It is currently locked in negotiations over further penalties following the appointment of an auditor

item.title: Hackers help themselves to 1Password's source code and customer data
item.description: 1Password is reassuring customers that their vaults remain secure after an attacker breached its systems and stole account information and private source code. The Canadian security biz disclosed this week that an attacker had compromised an employee's corporate GitHub account, made off with private source code, and deployed malicious code to its backend services to siphon off customer information. 1Password, which began investigating the intrusion on November 19, hasn't said how many customers were affected, but confirmed that the stolen data includes names and email addresses used to sign in to the service, account identifiers, timestamps showing when users created and last accessed their accounts, and various pieces of non-secret account metadata. The company insists the information that customers actually pay it to protect was beyond the intruder's reach. "At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker," 1Password said. Arguably more troubling is the revelation that the intruder gained access to 1Password's continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) infrastructure, which houses credentials used to keep its products running. The company says it has rotated or revoked potentially exposed credentials and that neither its apps nor its browser extensions were affected. 1Password hasn't explained how access to an employee's GitHub account enabled the attacker to deploy malicious code to its backend services, nor has it detailed the extent of the attacker's access to its software build and distribution infrastructure. The company did not respond to The Register's questions. The miscreant also got their hands on tokens embedded in emails sent to some customers as part of account invitations, provisioning, and recovery processes. These tokens aren't enough to access an account on their own, according to 1Password, as users must also authenticate via single sign-on or enter a verification code sent to their registered email address. The company says it specifically notified the small number of users with affected provisioning or recovery processes underway. It found no internal evidence of account takeovers using the exposed provisioning tokens. Still, the breach has prompted the password management biz to beef up those verification codes, replacing the six-digit numeric variety with ten-character alphanumeric codes to make brute-forcing them considerably more difficult. 1Password has booted the intruder out of its GitHub environment, revoked the stolen token, and rolled back the affected backend services to clean versions of the code. It's since shored up security around its development infrastructure and employees' devices, and brought in outside security specialists to review its handiwork. The incident recalls the first stage of LastPass's 2022 breach, when an attacker compromised its development environment and stole source code. item.title: Space plants with hot sauce: What ISS astronauts will be eating on Thanksgiving (video)
item.description: null The astronauts on the International Space Station will celebrate Thanksgiving with some nontraditional fare. Well, NASA astronaut Anil Menon will, anyway. In a video the agency released on Monday (Nov. 23), Menon showed off some of the plants he and his crewmates are growing in orbit and told us what's in store for the greens. "We need plants to survive as we set up our moon base , and as we go to Mars , we're going to have to grow our own nutrition. So that's what we're doing this Thanksgiving," Menon said in the 2.5-minute video. Astronauts deliver a Thanksgiving message from the International Space Station in November 2026. From left: NASA's Luke Delaney and Anil Menon, the Canadian Space Agency's Joshua Kutryk and NASA's Jessica Watkins. (Image credit: NASA) "I plan on using this [plant] with a tortilla and some pasta and some hot sauce to make my Thanksgiving meal," added Menon, who was wearing a chef's toque for the occasion. "And I'm grateful for you and for my family at home." He passed the microphone to fellow NASA astronaut Luke Delaney, who didn't talk about food but expressed gratitude to his family, crewmates and support network on Earth . Next up was NASA's Jessica Watkins, who gave us a rundown of the broader Thanksgiving menu in space. "Some of what we'll be eating here — we've got some roasted turkey, some mac and cheese, some mashed potatoes, and some candied yams," Watkins said, showing off the small bags containing each of those comestibles. "So, we should be in good shape." The Canadian Space Agency 's (CSA) Joshua Kutryk spoke next. He said he'll eat rice and the space-grown plants, which he'll consume raw "because it reminds me of Earth, which I miss." All four of the astronauts then wished us a happy Thanksgiving and did some zero-g flips and rolls, sending the space plants on a bit of a ride. Delaney, Kutryk and Watkins are members of SpaceX's Crew-13 mission, which arrived at the International Space Station (ISS) on Oct. 1 . There's a fourth Crew-13 astronaut as well — Sergey Teteryatnikov, of the Russian space agency Roscosmos . That quartet shares the ISS with Menon and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina, who arrived in July aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft. Astronauts tend to get major holidays off on the ISS, and to celebrate them together. Doing so reinforces the already-strong bonds the crewmates share and helps them deal with the pain of being away from friends and family, which can be especially acute on holidays like Thanksgiving and Christmas. Kutryk is likely feeling especially emotional these days. On Tuesday, the CSA announced that Kutryk's wife had given birth to the couple's third child, a daughter. "Even with the distance between us, we feel incredibly connected as we welcome our new little star into our lives," the couple said in a statement shared by the CSA. "We are very proud of our growing family and are looking forward to getting our little crew of five all reunited."

item.title: Mourners Mark Hong Kong Fire Anniversary, Authorities Warn Against ‘Disorder’
item.description: A stream of mourners laid flowers Thursday at the site of a horrific fire that ripped through a Hong Kong apartment complex and killed 168 people a year ago, with authorities warning against “acts of disorder”. The world’s deadliest residential building blaze since 1980 began on the afternoon of November 26, 2025 and raged for two days, gutting seven of Wang Fuk Court’s eight high-rise buildings that were home to some 4,600 people. Authorities in the Chinese territory — where Beijing has cracked down on dissent — appear wary of commemorations taking on a political tone and plan no official memorial. Police on Thursday kept a low profile as mourners laid hundreds of bouquets at a small park beneath the charred shells of the ruined buildings. They included former residents who stood on the same spot a year ago desperately waiting for news of their loved ones. “Families are torn apart, and people died,” said Koey Tam, a housewife and former resident in her 40s who lost her home, adding that they “can never be compensated with a new flat and a huge sum of money”. Smoke rises from apartments after a major fire swept through several blocks at the Wang Fuk Court residential estate in Hong Kong’s Tai Po district on November 27, 2025. (Photo by DALE DE LA REY / AFP) The government was “a bit cold” to hold no official memorials, she added. “What can a memorial event possibly affect?” Grace Chan, 69, expressed her frustration at what she called people’s “self-censorship”, telling reporters that “at first, I thought they’d given us a large space” to pay respects to the victims. “Too many Hongkongers remain silent,” she said, as she left a single chrysanthemum at the site. Former resident Dorz Cheung told AFP that he still felt “very, very, very angry” about the government’s response to oversights exposed in the tragedy. “There are still so many emotions… anger, deep sadness, they’re all around.” ‘Seeking Accountability’ A mourner brings flowers to Wang Fu Court in Hong Kong on November 26, 2026, the site of a horrific fire that ripped through seven apartment blocks and killed 168 people a year before. (Photo by Peter PARKS / AFP) The blaze was Hong Kong’s worst disaster in more than seven decades, and a shock to the 7.5 million residents of one of Asia’s safest cities. The city’s number two official Eric Chan said the government will offer help to “lawful” memorial events, but warned against “acts of disorder”. The Chinese government’s Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office spoke this week against attempts to “cause chaos” under the guise of commemorations. According to media reports, some local journalists have faced internal pressure when covering the fire, including to shelve programmes originally scheduled to go on air. A government spokesperson told AFP that as long as it is “within the law”, there are “no restrictions on the freedom to comment and criticise government policies for media outlets”.
